This summary aims to give you an overview of the information contained in this prospectus. As
this is a summary, it does not contain all the information that may be important to you. You should
read this prospectus in its entirety before you decide to invest in the Offer Shares. In particular , we
are a specialist technology company seeking to list on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock
Exchange under Chapter 18C of the Listing Rules because we are unable to meet the requirements
under Rule 8.05 (1), (2) or (3) of the Listing Rules. There are unique challenges, risks and
uncertainties associated with investing in companies such as ours. In addition, we have incurred
operating loss since our inception, and we may incur adjusted net loss (non-IFRS measure) and
operating loss for the foreseeable future. We had negative net cash flow generated from operating
activities during the Track Record Period. We did not declare or pay any dividends during the Track
Record Period and may not pay any dividends in the foreseeable future. Your investment decision
should be made in light of these considerations.
There are risks associated with any investment. Some of the particular risks in investing in the
Offer Shares are set out in “Risk Factors.” You should read that section carefully before you decide
to invest in the Offer Shares.
OVERVIEW
We are a leading domestic provider of high-performance automotive-grade SoCs, delivering
comprehensive automotive intelligence solutions that power key intelligent vehicle functions, from
intelligent cockpit to mid- to high-level advanced driver assistance. Our strategic focus lies in the design
and development of advanced automotive-grade SoCs and solutions.
We have focused on AI-powered
cockpits and the integration of cockpit and driving functionalities. We are the No. 1 domestic supplier in
the automotive SoC market in China in 2025, in terms of installation volume of intelligent cockpit domain
controller SoCs, according to Frost & Sullivan. Leveraging our system-level design approach enabling

without compromising on cost or efficiency. Our

platform.
Through in-house technological innovation and close collaboration with automotive OEMs and
tier-one suppliers, we continuously refine our products and drive their adoption across major automotive
platforms.
The global automotive industry is undergoing a fundamental transition toward digital and AI-driven
intelligent cockpits, centralized electrical and electronic (“ E/E”) architectures and ADAS powered by
multi-modal perception and large AI models. As vehicle intelligence accelerates, demand for high-
performance automotive-grade SoCs is
expanding, and SoCs will become the core computing engine
defining next-generation vehicle experience and competitiveness. At the same time, industrial intelligence
is shifting computation from cloud to edge, where low-latency, secure and power-efficient AI processing
is essential. This trend makes heterogeneous high-integration SoCs the foundational compute platform for
emerging robotics and edge AI applications. SiEngine was born out of the firm belief in this industry-wide
transformation. Our core team is composed of veterans from leading global semiconductor companies
with
expertise in advanced computing chips across automotive, server, and high-performance computing
applications. Leveraging this experience, they anticipated the growing demand for high-performance chips
in the automotive sector driven by the rise of intelligent vehicles. Since our inception, we have focused
on developing
automotive-grade SoCs using the latest processing techniques, such as the advanced 7nm
process, to deliver advanced compute capacity, energy efficiency and integration density. Recognizing that
the stringent requirements applicable to automotive-grade applications are similarly critical in industrial
automation and edge computing scenarios, we have strategically extended the application of our
automotive-grade SoCs to these adjacent high-growth markets. Leveraging a unified architecture and
reusable modules, we are able to efficiently adapt our solutions to meet the reliability, performance and
environmental demands of industrial deployments. This forward-looking strategy has enabled us to
rapidly
penetrate the market with a scalable, reusable product portfolio.

OUR PRODUCTS AND SOLUTIONS
We are a leading domestic provider of high-performance automotive-grade SoCs . We operate a
fabless model, under which we outsource the manufacturing, assembly and testing of our SoCs to wafer
foundries and OSA T service providers. Our product portfolio comprises our intelligent cockpit SoCs,
ADAS SoCs, AI accelerator SoCs, and industrial-grade SoCs.
Our products and solution are constructed on a system-level framework that integrates our core
capabilities in unified SoC design, foundational software platform, and comprehensive ecosystem support.
All of our SoCs are developed under a unified and high-performance architecture, which ensures high
on-chip integration and enables cross-domain functionality, while allowing us to
build differentiated
product portfolio. In addition, we provide a foundational software platform, comprising multi-OS
integration, BSP
and a suite of development tools, ensuring seamless integration and an efficient fit for
diverse customer needs. This comprehensive approach enables efficient development and deployment of
our products across diverse vehicle platforms.
Commercialization
We are dedicated to accelerating the commercialization of our automotive-grade SoCs and solutions.
Since we launched SE1000, including its trimmed version, SE500, in December 2021 and commenced the
mass production in March 2023, SE1000 had cumulative shipment volume of exceeding 1,550,000 units
as of December 31, 2025. We began generating revenue from sales of engineering samples for testing and
validation purposes of our industrial-grade SoCs and solutions in October 2023, which was formally
launched in July 2024 and became eligible for mass production in July 2024. We have adopted a
transaction-based model for our products and solutions. The following table illustrates the timeline of our

Intelligent Cockpit SoCs
Our intelligent cockpit SoC portfolio spans a full range of scenarios from entry-level to premium
intelligent cockpits, and from integrated cockpit-driving-parking solutions to next-generation cockpit-
driving fusion. Our flagship product, SE1000, is China’s first 7nm automotive-grade intelligent cockpit
SoC, breaking the long-standing dominance of international suppliers in this segment. Built on advanced
7nm process technology, SE1000 delivers high computing power, high integration, low power
consumption and
security, benchmarking closely against global flagship peers. Having adopted a
forward-looking architecture with dedicated interfaces and functional modules for NPU integration, the
standard version of our SE1000 enables cockpit-driving-parking integration, representing the industry’s
first high-value, all-in-one cockpit-driving-parking solution. We have also launched a trimmed version of
SE1000, namely our SE500, targeting basic intelligent cockpit applications. SE500 offers a cost-effective
solution for entry-level vehicle segments while maintaining the core capabilities of our flagship
architecture, enabling us to address the diverse performance and cost requirements from entry-level to
premium vehicle segments. SE2000 is our next-generation intelligent cockpit SoC, which is expected to
rival international cockpit chips, enabling both AI-powered intelligent cockpit experiences and seamless
cockpit-driving fusion. Manufactured using a 5nm automotive-grade process node, SE2000 is designed for
multi-modal interaction and edge AI inference, and delivers improved computing performance compared
to our current-generation products. SE2000 features next-generation advanced NPU and GPU, enabling
rich in-cabin visual experiences and advanced AI acceleration.
ADAS SoCs
Our ADAS SoC portfolio is designed to support a comprehensive range of assisted driving scenarios,
from L2 assisted driving to highway and urban Navigate on Autopilot (“ NOA”), full-scenario autonomous
driving, and advanced cockpit-driving fusion. AD1000 is a high-performance automotive-grade SoC built
on 7nm process technology and a heterogeneous multi-core architecture that delivers computation capacity
with native LLM support. AD1000 delivers NPU performance of 512 TOPS, and can scale up to 2,048
TOPS via multi-chip cascading. Eligible for mass production in 2025, AD1000 is positioned to provide the
core computing foundation for the widespread adoption of advanced autonomous driving capabilities
.
AD2000 is envisioned as the cerebral brain of future intelligent vehicles, delivering higher computing
capabilities and enhanced integration of compute and storage resources to lay the technical groundwork
for L3, L4 and higher levels of autonomous driving.
AI Accelerator SoCs
Our NNA100 is an edge AI chip simultaneously meeting automotive-grade requirements and
functional safety standards, which expects to obtain AEC-Q100 Grade 3 qualification and ISO 26262
ASIL-B certification. NNA100 is positioned as a high-efficiency AI co-processor that provides
customizable AI computing power for intelligent cockpit , as well as industrial and edge computing
scenarios, enabling optimized performance for specific application scenarios. With rich high-speed
interfaces that support multi-chip cascading, NNA100 can be deployed as a standalone AI compute module
or co-work with our intelligent cockpit as well as other mainstream processors, providing the AI
computing performance required to power intelligent cockpit applications in modern vehicles.
Industrial-Grade SoCs
We are extending our expertise in high-performance chips design to applications beyond the
automotive industry. Built on a high-performance general-purpose architecture, our chips are readily
extendable beyond automotive scenarios and spans a broad range of industry sectors,
supporting emerging
industrial and consumer scenarios, including embodied intelligence, advanced industrial drones,
autonomous logistics vehicles, and high-end robotic vacuum systems. This enables efficient reuse of our
core technologies and supports diversified and long-term sustainable growth across industries. We have
launched SE1000-I, extending our automotive-grade processor architecture, already validated under
stringent automotive standards, into industrial domains where reliability and safety are mission-critical.

SPECIALIST TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRIES
Our intelligent cockpit SoCs and solutions, ADAS SoCs and solutions and AI accelerator SoCs and
solutions fall within the specialist technology industry acceptable sectors of the semiconductors (design:
logic and physical design, and validation and verification) and electric and autonomous vehicles
(development of enabling technologies for autonomous vehicles). Our industrial-grade SoCs and solutions
fall within the specialist technology industry acceptable sector of the semiconductors (design: logic and
physical design, and validation and verification).
Our industry consultant, Frost & Sullivan, confirms and our Directors are of the view that based on
the above, our Company meets the definition of a Specialist Technology Company under Chapter 18C of
the Listing Rules.
OUR COMPETITIVE STRENGTHS
We believe that the following strengths contribute to our
market position, ensuring our success and
distinguishing us from our competitors: (i) global pioneer in high-performance automotive-grade SoCs and
a leading automotive SoC provider in China; (ii) advanced, high-performance and reliable automotive-
grade SoCs; (iii) system-Level technologies designed to optimize total implementation costs; (iv) globally
proven product capabilities with growing international recognition; (v) strategic shareholder collaboration
fostering synergies and growths; and (vi) Visionary management and R&D team with industry expertise.
OUR STRATEGIES
We are committed to enhancing our industry position and achieving business growth through the
following strategic initiatives: (i) continue developing core technologies and advancing product iteration
to lead the evolution of next-generation computing platforms; (ii) deepen customer engagement and
broaden customer base; (iii) further enrich the industry ecosystem and solidify our industrial position; and
(iv) diversifying applications to unlock long-term growth trajectories.
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
Our R&D activities follow a staggered, multi-generation roadmap, balancing the enhancement of
existing products, active development of next-generation offerings, and exploration of cutting-edge
technologies. We provide reusable platforms and a unified software foundation, enabling smooth upgrades
across product generations while reducing rework and migration costs. While closely tracking emerging
trends such as generative and multi-modal AI, we remain committed to measurable improvements in
reliability, performance, and energy efficiency, validated against customer workloads and aligned with
functional safety and security processes
. Our R&D team consists of dedicated talents with profound
industry expertise, focusing on developing and commercializing our products and solutions which help
maintain our technological advantages and market competitiveness. Each of our core R&D team members
has more than 15 years of industry experience in engineering, with global working experience in reputable
technology companies, such as Freescale, AMD, Broadcom and NXP .

COMPETITION
The automotive-grade SoC market is characterized by rapid technological evolution, stringent
automotive quality and safety requirements, and high barriers to entry. International companies still
dominate the market by virtue of their first mover advantage, while domestic companies are accelerating
their catch-up efforts. We mainly compete with
intelligent cockpit and autonomous driving SoC providers,
general chip providers and automotive OEM self-developers. Despite the competition, we believe our
automotive-grade SoC product portfolio and our comprehensive solution delivery capabilities stand out
among our competitors. In particular, we believe our unified
architecture, comprehensive product coverage
spanning intelligent cockpit and ADAS applications, proven automotive-grade quality and reliability
credentials, and
collaborative relationships with leading automotive OEMs and tier-one suppliers further
differentiate us from our competitors.

BUSINESS SUSTAINABILITY AND PATH TO PROFITABILITY
We had achieved business growth but were loss-making during the Track Record Period. Our revenue
increased from RMB110.8 million in 2023 to RMB234.5 million in 2024 and further to RMB 341.8 million
in 2025 . However, we recorded loss for the year of RMB838.5 million, RMB910.1 million and RMB 904.0
million in 2023 , 2024 and 2025, respectively, and recorded adjusted net loss (non-IFRS measure) of
RMB673.4 million, RMB736.8 million and RMB 661.3 million in the same periods, respectively.
The development and commercialization of automotive-grade SoCs are characterized by significant
upfront investments and long product commercialization cycles . We incurred net losses during the Track
Record Period, primarily attributable to the following reasons: (i) significant upfront investment in R&D
initiatives; (ii) limited economies of scale; (iii) early commercialization of revenue-generating products
and pre-commercialization of pipeline products; (iv) substantial cost of revenue; and (v) dynamic pricing
and marketing strategy.
Despite our net loss positions throughout the Track Record Period, our proactive
endeavors in product commercialization and market expansion have contributed to our revenue growth
during the Track Record Period.
We believe we will be able to achieve profitability through a combination
of revenue growth, improvement in gross profit margin and enhanced operating leverage.
We expect that our revenue will grow further due to the following factors: (i) leveraging industry
growth potential; (ii) expanding our offerings for diversified applications; and (iii) expanding and
deepening engagement with automotive OEMs and tier-one suppliers. We expect these initiatives to
increase operating expenses and place pressure on short-term cash flows. However, we believe we can
achieve sustained revenue growth with diverse product offerings and expanded customer base.
We aim to improve our gross profit margin through disciplined cost management and enhanced
supply chain efficiency. While short-term costs may fluctuate due to supplier qualification processes and
initial collaboration expenses, we anticipate that a more optimized supply structure will contribute to
greater cost stability and potentially enhance gross margin performance over time.
During the Track Record Period, we incurred substantial operating expenses to support our business
growth. However, as our business scales, our operating expenses, defined as the sum of research and
development expenses, general and administrative expenses and selling and marketing expenses, as a
percentage of total revenue
continued to decrease. In the future, we will continue optimizing our research
and development as well as sales and administrative functions to support our long-term business growth,
and we expect that our operating expenses, as a percentage of our total revenue, to continue to decrease
as our business expands.

OUR SHAREHOLDING STRUCTURE
Our Single Largest Group of Shareholders
Immediately prior to the Global Offering, Mobile & Magic Limited (“ M&M”) held approximately
18.55% of our total issued share capital, being our single largest Shareholder. M&M is wholly owned by
Future Magic Capital Limited, which is wholly owned by ECARX Holdings Inc., a company listed on the
NASDAQ (ticker symbol: ECX) (“ECARX Holdings ”, together with its subsidiaries, “ ECARX Group ”).
Therefore, as of the Latest Practicable Date, M&M, Future Magic Capital Limited, and ECARX Holdings
are our Single Largest Group of Shareholders and collectively control approximately
18.55% of the voting
rights in our Company. According to publicly available information, Fu&Li Industrious Innovators
Limited held approximately 44.3% of the issued share capital of ECARX Holdings Inc., with such
shareholding carrying approximately 49.0% of the voting rights. Fu&Li Industrious Innovators Limited is
owned as to 1.00% by Minghao Group Limited, which is wholly-owned by Li Shufu (၅), and as to
99.00% by Industrious Innovators Limited, which is owned by a trust established for the benefit of Li
Shufu and his family. The shares held by Minghao Group Limited are voting shares, and the shares held
by Industrious Innovators Limited are non-voting shares. Accordingly, Li Shufu is solely entitled to
exercise the voting and dispositive power in respect of all ordinary shares held by Fu&Li Industrious
Innovators Limited as of the Latest Practicable Date.
Immediately following the completion the Global Offering, the Single Largest Group of
Shareholders will collectively control the exercise of approximately [ 15.76]% of the voting rights
(assuming the Over-Allotment Option is not exercised) of our Company and thus remain as our Single
Largest Group of Shareholders.

DIVIDENDS
After the completion of the Global Offering, we may distribute dividends in the form of cash or by
other means permitted by our Articles of Association and our dividend policy. As advised by our PRC
Legal Advisor, we may not distribute dividend while we have accumulated losses. A decision to declare
or to pay dividends in the future and the amount of dividends will be at the discretion of our Board or the
general meeting and will depend on a number of factors, including our results of operations, cash flows,
financial condition, payments by our subsidiaries of cash dividends to us, business prospects, statutory,
regulatory restrictions on our declaration and payment of dividends and other factors that our Board may
consider important. Any declaration and payment as well as the amount of dividends will be subject to our
constitutional documents and the relevant laws. Our Shareholders in a general meeting may approve any
declaration of dividends. We do not currently have a formal dividend policy or a fixed dividend payout
ratio. During the Track Record Period, no dividends were paid or declared by our Company or any of our
subsidiaries
According to the applicable PRC laws and our Articles of Association, we will pay dividends out of
our profit after tax only after we have made the following allocations: recovery of the losses incurred in

This glossary contains explanations of certain technical terms used in this prospectus. As
such, these terms and their meanings may not correspond to standard industry meanings or usage
of these terms.
“ADAS” advanced driver-assistance system, an integrated set of advanced
driver assistance technologies that utilize sensors, software and
control systems to enhance driving safety, improve vehicle
operation and support semi-autonomous functions
“AEC-Q100” AEC-Q100 standard, a set of rigorous requirements and tests that
electronic components must pass to ensure their suitability for use
in automotive applications. The AEC-Q100 standard is widely
recognized and adopted in the automotive industry and is an
important consideration in the design and manufacturing of
electronic components for automotive applications
“ASIL” automotive safety integrity level, a risk classification scheme
defined by ISO 26262, and there are four ASIL levels identified by
the standard, namely ASIL A, ASIL B, ASIL C and ASIL D, among
which ASIL D dictates the highest integrity requirements on the
product
“A TE” standard semiconductor automated test equipment
“automotive OEMs” a vehicle manufacturer that designs, develops and produces
complete vehicles under its own brand and is responsible for
vehicle-level architecture, component selection, system
integration, regulatory compliance and final product quality
“A VP” autonomous valet parking
“BEV” bird-eye view, an elevated view of an object or location from a
very steep viewing angle, creating a perspective as if the observer
were a bird in flight looking downwards
“BOM” bill of materials, meaning parts and materials in process which are
used in an original manufacturing process to compose final
products
“BSP” board support package, in the context of an SoC, BSP is like a
“starter kit” of essential software that helps the operating system
communicate directly with the specific hardware on the SoC
“CAGR” compound annual growth rate
“DDR” double data rate, a memory interface technology that enables data
to be transferred on both the rising and falling edges of the clock
signal, effectively doubling the data transfer rate compared to
single data rate memory operating at the same clock frequency

interface standard used to connect components like graphics cards,
SSDs, and NICs to a computer’s motherboard, offering fast data
transfer and scalable bandwidth through multiple lanes
“PHY” physical layer, the physical layer of a communication interface,
whether implemented as dedicated on-chip hardware logic within
an SoC or as part of a system-level interface, that is responsible for

rendering, preserving the original sensor output and pixel pattern
information for subsequent processing and conversion
“RSA” a widely used public-key cryptographic algorithm based on the
computational difficulty of factoring large integers
“RTOS” real-time operating system

tools and programs in one installable package
“SOA” service-oriented architecture, a software architecture approach in
which system functionalities are organized as modular, reusable
services that communicate with each other through well-defined
interfaces
“SoC” an integrated circuit that incorporates functionally diverse sub-
modules within a single chip, forming a complete system tailored
for specific application scenarios. Typically integrating multiple
heterogeneous components, an SoC combines elements such as
general-purpose processors, hardware-based codec units, baseband
processors, and other specialized functional blocks into a unified
silicon die

RISKS RELATING TO THE COMMERCIALIZATION OF OUR PRODUCTS AND SOLUTIONS
We derive a significant portion of our revenue from a limited number of customers, including
ECARX Group, and the loss of, or a significant reduction in, business from any major customer
could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We have been and expect to continue to be subject to customer concentration risk. A significant
portion of our revenue during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date was derived
from a relatively small number of customers, including ECARX Group. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, revenue
generated from ECARX Group for the sales of our SoCs accounted for 99.4%, 99.3% and 96.3% of our
total revenue from sales of SoCs, respectively; revenue generated from ECARX Group for our licensing
and development services accounted for 98.3%, 100.0% and 98.0% of our total revenue from our licensing
and development services, respectively; and revenue generated from ECARX Group for our technical
support services accounted for 100.0%, 68.6% and 81.8% of our total revenue from our technical support
services, respectively. As of the Latest Practicable Date, ECARX Group collectively held approximately
18.55 % of our total issued share capital. For details, see “Relationship with Our Single Largest Group of
Shareholders — Overview.” This high level of customer concentration exposes us to the risk that the loss
of, or a significant decrease in, sales to any one of our major customers could materially and adversely
affect our business. There is no assurance that ECARX Group or any other major customer will continue
to place orders with us at current or historical levels, or that they will not reduce or cease their use of our
products and solutions due to changes in strategic direction, internal R&D capabilities, product roadmaps,
cost considerations, or operational or financial performance. Tier-one suppliers, including ECARX, may
also choose to work with competing suppliers for future vehicle models, particularly as competition in the
intelligent cockpit and autonomous driving sectors intensifies and as more suppliers emerge with
cost-competitive offerings.
Furthermore, the nature of the automotive industry, particularly in China, is rapidly evolving, with
increasingly compressed product lifecycles, intensifying competition, and fast-changing consumer
demands. While we aim to expand our tier-one supplier and automotive OEM customer base, including
through ongoing efforts to secure adoption and deployment of our SoCs and mass production projects with
new domestic and overseas tier-one suppliers and automotive OEMs, there can be no assurance that we
will be successful in acquiring or retaining new customers on commercially favorable terms. In addition,
despite our efforts to expand our automotive OEM customer base, the possibility remains that the
automotive OEMs may select ECARX as their tier-one supplier, which may result in further revenue
concentration on ECARX Group. Any inability to diversify our customer base, reduce reliance on major
customers, or expand into new vehicle programs could limit our growth trajectory and make us more
vulnerable to adverse developments affecting our key customers. For details, see “Business — Customers
— Our Relationship with ECARX Group.” In light of the above, any reduction, delay, or termination of
business from ECARX Group or other major customers, whether due to strategic shifts, pricing changes,
project reallocations, or adverse developments in their own operations, could materially and adversely
affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Our results of operations are affected by seasonal fluctuations.

On October 28, 2024, the U.S. Department of the Treasury (the “Treasury”) issued the Provisions
Pertaining to U.S. Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of
Concern (the “Outbound Investment Rule”).
See “Business — International Sanctions and the U.S.
Outbound Investment Security Program — The Outbound Investment Security Program” for details. As
advised by our OIR and Export Control Legal Advisor, we may be deemed a “covered foreign person”
defined under the Outbound Investment Rule due to our business activities. The Outbound Investment
Rule prohibits investments by, or that are knowingly directed by, a U.S. person in us, as certain integrated
circuit we have designed that is not for data center use meets or exceeds the performance parameters in
Export Control Classification Number 3A090.a in supplement No. 1 to 15 CFR part 774; however, subject
to the apparent meaning or export controls classification interpretation, we could be also viewed as only
engaged in activities set out in the Notifiable Transaction category as defined in the Outbound Investment
Rule and U.S. persons could only be subjected to notification requirements rather than being prohibited
outright. As set out in the Outbound Investment Rules, U.S. persons are responsible for determining their
compliance with the rules, and the due diligence responsibilities lie on the U.S. person. Potential U.S.
person investors are therefore advised to consult independent legal advice on this matter prior to investing
in us.
On December 23, 2025, the Treasury published additional frequently asked questions (“FAQs”) on
the Outbound Investment Rule. One of these FAQs (X. 4) provides that absent additional facts, when a
U.S. person acquires an equity interest in a “covered foreign person,” and at the time of such acquisition
the equity interest is publicly traded, such security falls under the description of a “publicly traded
security” in 31 C.F.R. §850.501(a)(1)(i), regardless of when an agreement to make its investments is
entered into. In light of the FAQs’ guidance, as advised by our OIR and Export Control Legal Advisor, a
U.S. person’s acquisition of our H shares that are publicly listed and traded in this Global Offering may
constitute an “excepted transaction” assuming the U.S. person would not also be afforded rights beyond
“standard minority shareholder protections.” While neither the Outbound Investment Rule nor the FAQs
define the time of acquisition, as advised by our OIR and Export Control Legal Advisor, it is reasonable
to conclude that the acquisition of the H shares by investors occurs upon settlement with them since the
investors will receive our H shares at settlement. As long as the settlement of the H shares purchased by
U.S. persons occurs after 9:00 a.m. on the Listing Date, the H shares they acquire would be publicly listed
and traded securities. However, if settlement occurs before 9:00 a.m. on the Listing date when the H shares
are not yet publicly listed and traded (for example, this is the case for settlement for Hong Kong Offer
Shares), it remains uncertain whether the publicly traded securities exception under the Outbound
Investment Rule can be applicable. It is expected that U.S. persons will be able to purchase our H Shares
publicly traded on the Stock Exchange following the Global Offering without being subject to any
notification required or be outright prohibited based on the publicly traded securities exception, as long
as the investment made does not afford a U.S. person certain rights that are not standard minority
shareholder protections. Nevertheless, even though U.S. persons’ acquisitions of certain offer securities
(such as our publicly traded H shares) could be exempted from the scope of covered transactions, the
Outbound Investment Rule could still limit our ability to raise capital or contingent equity capital from
U.S. investors prior to and after this Global Offering given that relevant laws, regulations, and policies
continue to evolve. In addition, we cannot predict how the Outbound Investment Rule will be enforced,
and neither can we guarantee that there will not be an expansion to the scope of the Outbound Investment
Rule, a change in interpretation to broaden its application, or an enactment of similar laws or regulations
that impinge upon our business activities in the future. The uncertainty in the interpretation and
enforcement of the Outbound Investment Rule may reduce U.S. investors’ interest in our equity securities.
In such a case, the trading price and liquidity of our H Shares may be adversely affected. If our ability
to raise such capital is significantly and negatively affected, it could also be detrimental to our business,
financial condition and prospects.

W AIVER IN RESPECT OF JOINT COMPANY SECRETARIES
Pursuant to Rules 3.28 and 8.17 of the Listing Rules, the company secretary must be an individual
who, by virtue of their academic or professional qualifications or relevant experience, is, in the opinion
of the Stock Exchange, capable of discharging the functions of the company secretary. The Stock
Exchange considers the following academic or professional qualifications to be acceptable:
(i) a member
of The Hong Kong Chartered Governance Institute; (ii) a solicitor or barrister (as defined in the Legal
Practitioners Ordinance); and (iii) a certified public accountant (as defined in the Professional Accountants
Ordinance).
Pursuant to Note 2 to Rule 3.28 of the Listing Rules, in assessing “relevant experience,” the Stock
Exchange will consider the individual’s: (i) length of employment with the issuer and other issuers and the
roles they played; (ii) familiarity with the Listing Rules and other relevant laws and regulations including
the Securities and Futures Ordinance, the Companies Ordinance, the Companies (Winding Up and
Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance and the Takeovers Code;
(iii) relevant training taken and/or to be
taken in addition to the minimum requirement of taking not less than 15 hours of relevant professional
training in each financial year under Rule 3.29 of the Listing Rules; and
(iv) professional qualifications
in other jurisdictions.
Pursuant to paragraph 13 of Chapter 3.10 of the Guide for New Listing Applicants, the Stock
Exchange will consider a waiver application by an issuer in relation to Rules 3.28 and 8.17 of the Listing
Rules based on the specific facts and circumstances. Factors that will be considered by the Stock Exchange
include:
(i) length of employment with the issuer and other issuers and the roles they played; (ii) whether
the issuer has principal business activities primarily outside Hong Kong; (iii) whether the issuer was able
to demonstrate the need to appoint a person who does not have the Acceptable Qualification (as defined
under paragraph 11 of Chapter 3.10 of the Guide for New Listing Applicants) nor Relevant Experience (as
defined under paragraph 11 of Chapter 3.10 of the Guide for New Listing Applicants) as a company
secretary; and
(iv) why the directors consider the individual to be suitable to act as the issuer’s company
secretary.
Further, pursuant to paragraph 13 of Chapter 3.10 of the Guide for New Listing Applicants, such
waiver, if granted, will be for a fixed period of time (the “ Waiver Period ”) and on the following
conditions: (i) the proposed company secretary must be assisted by a person who possesses the
qualifications or experience as required under Rule 3.28 of the Listing Rules and is appointed as a joint
company secretary throughout the Waiver Period; and
(ii) the waiver will be revoked if there are material
breaches of the Listing Rules by the issuer.
Our Company considers that while it is important for the company secretary to be familiar with the
relevant securities regulation in Hong Kong, they also need to have experience relevant to our Company’s
operations, nexus to the Board and close working relationship with the management of our Company in
order to perform the function of a company secretary and to take the necessary actions in the most
effective and efficient manner. It is for the benefit of our Company to appoint a person who is familiar
with our Company’s business and affairs as company secretary.
We have appointed Mr. Hou Shifei (“ Mr. Hou ”) and Ms. Pun Kim Ying (“ Ms. Pun ”) as our joint
company secretaries. Mr. Hou is our vice president and manager of our listing-related matters and has
more than 33 years of experience in financial and capital market affairs. Since Mr. Hou does not possess
a qualification stipulated in Rule 3.28 of the Listing Rules, he is not able to solely fulfill the requirements
as a company secretary of a listed issuer stipulated under Rules 3.28 and 8.17 of the Listing Rules.
Notwithstanding the above, we consider the appointment of Mr. Hou appropriate and necessary, given that
he is familiar with the Group’s operations and corporate governance matters and had previously served as
the chief financial officer and the secretary of the Board at Baiwang Co., Ltd., a company listed on the

AUTOMOTIVE CHIPS INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Introduction of Automotive Chips
Automotive chips are a crucial component of modern vehicles. Unlike chips applied in consumer
electronics and industrial scenarios, automotive chips are designed specifically to meet the stringent
requirements of vehicular environments and widely used in areas such as cockpit systems, chassis,
powertrains, autonomous driver assistance systems, and body electronics. These chips must possess high
reliability, stability, and safety. In 202
5, the market size of global and China automotive chips reached
approximately RMB 463.6 billion and RMB 137.7 billion, respectively. The ongoing development of
automotive electrification and intelligence has resulted in a growing demand for chip usage and
performance, further driving the growth of the automotive chip market. It is expected that the global and
China automotive chip market will reach RMB
904.0 billion and RMB 315.4 billion by 20 30, respectively,
representing a significant growth opportunity for the market players.
Automotive chips can be classified into computing chips, memory chips, sensor chips,
communication chips, and power chips. Among various types of chips, computing chips have become the
current industry focus, referring to process the massive amounts of data generated by vehicles during
driving, interaction, and safety-related scenarios, and to support the implementation of various intelligent
functions. In 202
5, the market size of global and China automotive computing chips reached RMB 233.8
billion and RMB 69.5 billion, respectively. Driven by the surging demand for high-performance computing
chips amid automotive intelligentization, it is expected that the market size of global and China
automotive computing chips will reach RMB
510.8 billion and RMB 178.2 billion, respectively.
Evolution of Automotive Electrical & Electronic Architecture
Automotive Electrical & Electronic Architecture (EEA) refers to the solution integrating electronics
hardware, network communications, software applications and wiring that controls vehicle functions in the
areas of vehicle control, body and security, infotainment, active safety, and other comfort, convenience,
and connectivity functionality.
In traditional distributed automotive EEA, each ECU (Electronic Control Unit) is typically tasked
with controlling only one single functional unit. With the development of automotive intelligence,

Therefore, the automotive EEA is currently evolving from a distributed architecture toward a
domain-centralized architecture by application of DCU (Domain Control Unit). Leading companies have
initiated the deployment of cross-domain integration solutions, promoting technical integration between
different functional domains such as the cockpit domain and autonomous driving domain. These advanced
EEA can effectively reduce the overall vehicle mass, lower R&D costs, shorten the development cycle, and
ensure vehicle performance.

Impact of Automotive Electrical & Electronic Architecture Evolution on Automotive Chips
MCU and SoC are two typical types of computing chips that have a profound impact on EEA design.
In ECU, the core computing chip — MCU, refers to a type of traditional circuit design that contains only
a single CPU (central processing unit) as the processor. In domain controller, the computing chip — SoC
stands for System-on-Chip, which is a type of integrated circuit design that combines all the necessary
components and subsystems required for a specific application or function into a single microchip. This
includes components such as the CPU, GPU (Graphics Processing Unit), FPGA (Field Programmable Gate
Array), ASIC (Application-specific Integrated Circuit), NPU (Neutral Processing Unit) and others.
As SoC integrates a greater number of heterogeneous processing units, it boasts more sophisticated
architectural designs and delivering enhanced processing and computational capabilities. Their defining
characteristics — high performance, low power consumption, compact form factor, and high reliability —
render them particularly well-suited for multi-task processing and applications with increasingly complex
computational requirements, such as cockpit systems, autonomous driving systems and other functions.

increasingly prominent, owing to their significant advantages in computing performance, data

Automotive SoC Industry Chain Analysis
The upstream of China’s automotive SoC industry chain includes key areas such as semiconductor
intellectual property (IP), wafer fabrication, packaging and testing, and electronic design automation
(EDA) software.
The midstream segment comprises automotive SoC Companies, which are responsible for the
definition, design, and adaptation of SoC products. This requires them to possess advanced expertise in
semiconductor technology, a profound understanding of automotive intelligent functions, and robust
capabilities in adapting to other hardware and software components. The majority of players in the market
are SoC provider, which offer their SoC products directly and without constraints to tier-1 suppliers or
OEMs. By contrast, only a very few companies operate as system providers, which supply OEMs with
system-level solutions integrated with their SoC products.
The downstream segment includes tier-one suppliers that provide comprehensive intelligent
solutions to automotive OEMs. In recent years, Chinese domestic automakers have been leading the global
wave of intelligentization, with their product competitiveness continuously improving. From 2020 to
2024, the market share of Chinese domestic automotive brands in the domestic market rose significantly
from 40% to 58.5%. Driven by demands for supply chain security and data security, Chinese automotive
OEMs have an increasingly strong demand for domestic substitution of high-performance and high-end
chips.

Cost and Price of SoC
The cost differences among SoCs vary significantly depending on their performance, application
scenarios, and manufacturing processes. Among these cost components, wafer fabrication is the most
significant, accounting for approximately 70% to 80% of the total SoC cost, while the remaining costs are
mainly composed of packaging and testing. The prices of SoCs also vary considerably depending on their
application scenarios, performance, and cost factors. Generally, the price range of SoCs spans from a few

Drivers of Automotive SoC Market
 Consumers Show Increased Preference for Intelligent Features
In recent years, the level of intelligentization has become one of the key decision-making factors for
consumers when choosing vehicle models and brands, with many willing to pay a premium for advanced
intelligent features. Driven by this trend, automakers are rapidly increasing their investment in
intelligentization R&D and accelerating the launch of intelligent vehicle models. As technology advances
and costs decrease, for example, highly integrated solutions such as “cockpit-parking integration” or
“cockpit-driving fusion” can effectively reduce costs, helping automakers quickly deploy their intelligent
features to mid-to-low-end models and thereby cover a broader market. In 202
5, passenger vehicles priced
between RMB100,000 and 200,000 accounted for 49.6% of total sales. As sophisticated intelligent
functionalities further penetrate this price segment in the future, market demand for SoCs will grow
rapidly.
 Technological Advancements Drive Demand for High-Performance SoCs
Upgrades in intelligent cockpit functions, rapid iteration of autonomous driving technologies, and
the growing application of AI are driving automotive electronics to adopt higher-performance SoCs. For
instance, back in 2020, the CPU computing power required for intelligent cockpits mostly fell within the
range of 20—50 KDMIPS, while the AI computing power required for autonomous driving was mostly
under 20 TOPS. As demand continues to escalate, mainstream intelligent cockpit SoCs today need to
deliver computing power in the range of 80-200 KDMIPS; and the computing power of mainstream
autonomous driving SoCs generally reaches over 100 TOPS. High-performance SoCs command premium
pricing and accelerate growth in the SoC value per-vehicle, as well as the overall market size by meeting
intelligent vehicles’ rising technical demands.
 National Policies Drive Development of China Automotive Chip Industry
In recent years, the development of China’s automotive chip industry has received significant
attention at the national level. Multiple policy documents have explicitly supported the growth of the
automotive chip industry. For example, policy initiatives such as the Guidelines for the Construction of
the National Automotive Chip Standard System and the Development Plan for the New Energy V ehicle
Industry (2021-2035) clearly emphasize the need to break through key technologies in automotive chips
and intelligent computing platforms. In addition, the government has provided targeted financial support
key companies across chip design, manufacturing, and packaging & testing, thereby alleviating R&D
funding pressures. It has also reduced corporate income tax for high-tech enterprises, enhanced deductions
for R&D expenses, and exempted imported equipment from custom duties.

Trends of Automotive SoC Market
 Artificial Intelligence Development Reshapes the Automotive Intelligence
With the deepening application of generative AI and AI Agent technologies in automotive scenarios,
the automotive intelligence is transitioning from functional interaction to an AI driven era of proactive
service. Surging demand for natural language understanding, multi-modal perception, personalized
recommendations, and real-time decision-making capabilities necessitates the deployment of large
language models or specialized AI models with tens of billions of parameters within vehicles. This
presents unprecedented challenges for automotive SoCs in terms of computing density, memory
bandwidth, and energy efficiency. To address this, next-generation cockpit SoCs are increasingly
integrating dedicated AI acceleration units, such as NPUs, TPUs, or AI computing engines, to enable edge
device model inference, ensuring fast response times and data security. This trend is significantly driving
up both the demand for and the value of high-performance automotive SoCs per vehicle.
 Chinese Automotive SoC Providers Participate in Global Market Competition
Leveraging strong technical strength and service capabilities, leading Chinese SoC providers have
successfully entered the global vehicle supply chains of major international automotive OEM, securing
projects for multi global vehicle models. These SoC providers are not only meeting functional
requirements of global market but also adhering to multiple international standards from the early product
design phase, ensuring their chip solutions comply with regulatory and certification requirements in
different regions. As their global footprint deepens, Chinese automotive SoC providers are poised to
compete comprehensively with traditional automotive chip giants on the international stage, reshaping the
global landscape of the automotive chip market.

 Establishment of Chinese Automotive SoC Ecology

time-to-market for customer products, and strengthens the competitiveness of Chinese automotive SoCs
in global market.

Entry Barriers of Automotive SoC Market
 Technical Barriers
The technological barriers for automotive SoCs are reflected in multi-dimensional and stringent
requirements. First, a high-level R&D team is essential, requiring the integration of cross disciplinary
talents in chip architecture design, automotive-grade algorithm optimization, AI, and embedded system
development. Second, the industry demands decades of technical accumulation, necessitating a
comprehensive technology system spanning from chip design to failure analysis.
 Ecological Barriers
The core of ecosystem barriers lies in deep collaboration with automotive OEMs and comprehensive
chain-wide management capabilities. Chip companies must engage in vehicle planning up to two years in
advance, engineering key parameters such as computing power allocation and interface protocols based on
the vehicle’s EEA and feature lists for intelligent cockpit and autonomous driving systems. This demands
strong product definition capabilities from chip manufacturers, spanning multiple layers including
operating systems, middleware, and application software, requiring them to deliver not only high-
performance hardware but also robust software support and service capabilities.
 Certification Barriers
Automotive chips face strict certification barriers to enter the automotive supply chain, with several
international standards forming core thresholds. The AEC-Q standards regulate chip reliability and
durability through rigorous environmental stress tests like temperature cycling and vibration resistance.
ISO 26262 mandates functional safety measures with ASIL-level compliance, covering full lifecycle risk
control from design to production. IA TF 16949 requires standardized manufacturing processes and quality
traceability systems. These certifications demand substantial technical validation and resource investment,
resulting in a typical certification cycle in years and creating significant market entry barriers for new
players.
 Investment Barriers
Automotive chip development faces high investment barriers, imposing stringent requirements on
capital strength and long-term planning capabilities. Take high-performance automotive-grade SoCs as an
example: the development phase alone requires an investment of multi-billion RMB, covering core costs
such as IP , EDA, R&D team expense, tape-out and testing. Coupled with the need for continuous
investment in technology iteration and equipment upgrades during the lengthy 3-4 year development cycle,
the high and long-term capital pressure serving as a significant barrier for new players entering the field.
Challenges of Automotive SoC Market
Stringent requirements for functional safety, reliability and system security remain key challenges to
the automotive SoC market. In addition, long vehicle qualification cycles, high development investment
and continuous technology upgrades may prolong product commercialization and affect development
efficiency.

Definition of Intelligent Cockpit
The cockpit is an integrated space within a vehicle that combines driving control, human-machine
interaction, information display, riding comfort, and functional services, serving as the core area for direct
interaction between users and the vehicle. The evolution of automotive cockpits has unfolded across

distinct stages: from the electronic cockpits of the past, to today’s intelligent cockpits, and onward to
AI-powered cockpits, which are widely recognized as the next frontier in development.
Electronic cockpit: the early digital form of automotive cockpits. In essence, it replaces traditional
mechanical controls with electronic devices to achieve basic human-vehicle interaction. Since each
functional module operates independently, there is no need for high-performance chips for unified
computing or data integration; only simple microcontrollers are required to handle basic control of
individual modules.
Intelligent cockpit: as the next generation of the electronic cockpit, centers on high performance
SoCs, paired with operating systems and software algorithms. It enables data interconnection, computing
power allocation, and functional collaboration among multiple in-cockpit devices, integrating navigation,
entertainment, communication, and other functions to deliver more convenient, comfortable, and
personalized experiences for drivers and passengers.
AI-powered intelligent cockpit: Aided by AI agents, intelligent cockpits will evolve into
AI-powered intelligent cockpits. SoCs with greater computing power will provide hardware support for AI
computations, while large models will be capable of understanding drivers’ behavioral habits, preferences,
and real-time needs to deliver personalized services. Equipped with stronger autonomous learning
capabilities, AI-powered cockpits will continuously optimize user experiences over time and contribute to
enhanced safety.
Definition of Intelligent Cockpit SoC
The intelligent Cockpit SoC is a core processor chip specifically designed for automotive intelligent
cockpit systems, responsible for driving the efficient operation of various interactive, entertainment,
information display, and multi-device collaboration functions within the cockpit. Its core role is to
integrate multiple in-cockpit modules, such as instrument clusters, central control screens, head-up
displays (HUD), voice interaction, in-vehicle entertainment, and connected car services, through robust
computing power, multimedia processing capabilities, and multi-interface compatibility, thereby enabling
intelligent, scenario-based, and personalized human-machine interaction.
For instance, it needs to support functions like high-definition multi-screen linkage (e.g., information
sharing between instrument clusters and central control screens), natural language processing (recognition
and feedback of voice commands), biometric identification (driver status monitoring), and smooth
operation of in-vehicle OS systems. Meanwhile, it must meet the requirements of low power consumption
and high stability in automotive environments to deliver an immersive and convenient cockpit experience
for users.

and scenario-based functional innovations. The sales volume of vehicle equipped with intelligent cockpits

AUTONOMOUS DRIVING SOC INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Definition of Autonomous Driving
Autonomous driving technology refers to a comprehensive system that leverages sensors, cameras,
radars, positioning systems, and artificial intelligence algorithms to enable vehicles to perceive their
surroundings, plan routes, and execute control functions with minimal or no human intervention, thereby
completing driving tasks. Autonomous driving technology is categorized into six level, from Level 0 to
Level 5. At present, autonomous driving technology is undergoing a transitional phase from L2 to L3, as
it continues to develop towards higher levels of automation.
L1-L2 technology has already achieved
large-scale commercialization. In contrast, L3 and above technology has yet to see large-scale application
and is currently operating on a limited scale in closed or semi-closed environments, such as commercial
vehicles, port logistics, and mining sites-or in passenger vehicles as pilot programs.
Definition of Autonomous Driving SoC
Autonomous driving SoC is a type of SoC specifically designed for autonomous driving
functionalities, serve as the “central brain” of an autonomous driving vehicle. The implementation of
autonomous driving generally involves three core layers: perception, decision-making, and execution.
Operating within the decision-making layer, autonomous driving SoC is responsible for processing and
fusing data collected by sensors in the perception layer, then generating driving decisions to replace human
intervention.
Global and China Autonomous Driving Vehicle Market
Autonomous driving technology has played a pivotal role in driving safety of vehicles by minimizing
driver errors and reducing the risk of traffic accidents. Driven by advancements in in-vehicle computing
performance and the growing reliance of consumers on advanced driver assistance features, the global
autonomous driving passenger vehicle market continues to expand. Global sales increased from
28 million
units in 2021 to 59.2 million units in 2025, with a CAGR of 20.6%, and are projected to reach 84.5 million
units by 2030. In China, benefiting from the rapid penetration of autonomous configurations in new
models and the accelerated mass deployment of autonomous driving features by automakers, sales rose
from 9.2 million units in 2021 to 21.7 million units in 2025, with a CAGR of 24.0% over the period, with
the figure expected to reach 27.2 million units by 2030.
Global and China Autonomous Driving SoC Market
In line with the development of autonomous driving vehicles, the global market size of autonomous
driving SoC increased from RMB 13.9 billion to RMB 59.8 billion from 2021 to 2025, representing a
CAGR of 44.1%. This growth was primarily fueled by the widespread adoption of L2 autonomous driving
functions in mid-to-high-end passenger vehicles and the mass production of automotive high-performance
chips. From 202
6t o 2030, the global market is expected to maintain strong momentum, growing at a
CAGR of 18.3% to reach RMB 161.0 billion by 2030.
Driven by the rapid integration of high-performance chips into mid-to-high-end models by domestic
new energy vehicle manufacturers and autonomous driving solution providers, as well as the accelerated
mass production of domestic automotive SoCs, the growth rate of China’s autonomous driving SoC market
has outpaced the global average. From
2021 to 2025, the market size in China expanded from RMB 5.5
billion to RMB 32.5 billion . Against the backdrop of rapidly increasing autonomous driving penetration,
faster in-house hardware and software development by automotive OEMs, and the accelerated installation

16.5% from
2026t o 2030, and reaching RMB 82.0 billion by 2030. In terms of installation volume, global and China
autonomous driving SoCs amounted to 39.4 million units and 13.3 million units, respectively, in 2025, and
are expected to reach to 78.1 million units and 26.4 million units, respectively, by 2030.

Global and China Industrial SoC Chip Market
Driven by the global wave of industrial intelligence upgrades and the accelerated adoption of AI
applications, the global industrial SoC chip market has maintained steady expansion, with its size
increasing from RMB
6.6 billion in 2021 to RMB 12.9 billion in 2025, with a CAGR of 18.2% from 2021
to 2025, and is projected to reach RMB 29.4 billion by 2030. Benefiting from the digital transformation
of the domestic manufacturing sector and the rising penetration of AI applications, the Chinese market size

2.4 billion in 2021 to RMB 4.7 billion in 2025, with a CAGR of 18.0% from 2021 to 2025,

industrial SoC chips reached 85.0 million units and 45.9 million units, respectively, in 2025, and are

Market Driver and Trends of Industrial SoC chip Market
The growth of the industrial SoC chip market is driven by three key factors: industrial intelligence
upgrades, the penetration of edge computing, and the commercialization of embodied intelligence.
Industrial sectors like manufacturing and energy are adopting high-automation scenarios, boosting demand
for high-performance, low-latency industrial SoC chips that optimize control and energy management,
propelling industrial high-end transformation. The massive time-sensitive data generated by intelligent
industrial devices makes centralized computing inadequate, and industrial SoCs, with their low-latency
and on-device inference advantages, have become core engines for edge computing, accelerating their
market penetration. Meanwhile, the embodied intelligence industry, which is in the pre-stage of large-scale
commercialization, relies on high-performance SoCs for data processing and intelligent decision-making,
and its future development will significantly expand the application scope of the SoC market.
Challenges of Industrial SoC Chip Market
Maintaining stable and reliable operation over extended service cycles and under demanding
industrial environments represents a key challenge to the industrial SoC chip market. In addition,
fragmented application scenarios, stringent reliability standards and long-term supply and support
requirements may increase development complexity and affect the pace of market adoption.

REGULATORY ENVIRONMENT IN THE PRC
The following provides an overview of the major PRC laws, regulations, and policies related to the
Company’s current daily business operations in the PRC.
Policies Related to the Integrated Circuit Industry
In June 2014, the State Council promulgated the Outline for Promoting the Development of the
National Integrated Circuit Industry, which stated that the development goal of the integrated circuit
industry is to reach an advanced international standard in the major links of the integrated circuit industry
chain by 2030, with a number of enterprises entering the international first tier and achieving leapfrog
development. One of the main tasks and development priorities
is to focus on the development of
integrated circuit design industry when strengthening collaborative innovation in integrated circuit design,
software development, system integration, content and services based on the industrial chain in key areas
so as to drive the manufacturing industry developing with the rapid growth of the design industry.
In July 2020, the State Council announced the Several Policies for Promoting High Quality
Development of the Integrated Circuit Industry and the Software Industry in the New Era. To further
optimize the development environment for the integrated circuit and software industries, deepen
international industrial cooperation, and enhance industrial innovation capabilities and development
quality, a series of supportive policies
were introduced.
In March 2021, the NPC promulgated the Outline of the 14th Five-Y ear Plan for National Economic
and Social Development and the Long-Range Objectives through the Y ear 2035 of the PRC, which
outlined plans to cultivate advanced manufacturing clusters. The plan emphasizes innovation and
development in industries such as integrated circuits
.
In December 2021, the State Council promulgated the Notice of the State Council on Issuing the 14th
Five-Y ear Plan for the Development of the Digital Economy, which clarified that during the “14th
Five-Y ear Plan” period, the promotion of digital industrialization should be accelerated to make up for key
technical shortcomings
, focusing on breakthroughs in key core technologies in the fields of high-end
chips, operating systems, industrial software and frameworks. In addition, the competitiveness of key links
in the industrial chain should be improved, and the supply chain systems of key industries such as
integrated circuits, artificial intelligence, and industrial Internet should be improved.
In January 2024, seven departments including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
(the “MIIT”) promulgated the Implementation Opinions of Seven Departments Including the Ministry of
Industry and Information Technology on Promoting the Innovative Development of Industries of the
Future, which identifies the breakthrough of high-level intelligent connected vehicle technology and the
development of iconic intelligent connected vehicle products as one of the key tasks.
In August 2025, the MIIT and the
SAMR promulgated the Action Plan for Stabilizing Growth of the
Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry (2025-2026), which emphasizes that sustained support will
be provided for scientific and technological innovation in areas including integrated circuits and new
industrial control systems. The Plan stipulates that the development of automotive electronics and related
industries shall be supported, so as to propel the sector’s digital transformation and intelligent upgrading.
In September 2025, Eight departments including the MIIT promulgated the Work Plan for Ensuring
Stable Growth in the Automotive Sector (2025-2026). The Plan calls for pushing forward high-quality
development of the automotive industry, improving the market environment, strengthening oversight,
boosting new-energy vehicle uptake and refining the policy support framework. Within its provisions,
technological innovation is to be harnessed to unlock latent consumer demand, breakthroughs in
vehicle-grade chips,
etc. are to be accelerated, and the recruitment of high-calibre professionals is to be
intensified in the key domains of automotive chips, operating systems and basic materials.

Standards and Specifications Related to Automotive Chip Design
According to the Failure Mechanism Based Stress Test Qualification for Integrated Circuits
(AEC-Q100) established by the Automotive Electronics Council (AEC), its latest valid version is Rev-J,
released in 2023. It is widely used as a baseline for the reliability stress testing of automotive integrated
circuits . It requires devices to undergo a range of stress tests, including environmental, lifetime, and
electrical tests, to evaluate product reliability.
According to Road vehicles — Functional safety (ISO 26262) established by the International
Organization for Standardization (ISO), its latest valid version is ISO 26262:2018 (Second Edition). It
applies to electrical and electronic systems and software within the automotive sector. It provides
requirements and process specifications for functional safety throughout the product lifecycle, defining
functional safety goals and associated design requirements for varying ASIL grades from A to D.
According to the Guidelines for the Construction of the National Automotive Chip Standard System
released by the MIIT in December 2023, the document outlines an automotive chip standard system
covering basic general standards, product and technology application standards, and supporting test
standards. It proposes overall requirements for key areas such as environmental reliability,
electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), functional safety, and information security, and describes technical
specifications for automotive chip products (e.g., control, computing, sensing, communication, and
storage) and related test standards. It also sets phased goals to develop more than 30 key standards by 2025
and more than 70 by 2030, aiming to achieve broad coverage of typical scenarios and test methods.
Regulations Related to Foreign Investment in the PRC
Regulations on Corporation
According to the Company Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from July 1, 2024, the
“Company Law”), promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (the
“NPCSC”)
, limited liability companies and joint-stock limited companies established within the territory
of China are subject to the Company Law. Unless otherwise specified by the laws and regulations on
foreign investment, foreign-invested enterprises are also governed by the Company Law.
Foreign Investment Regulation
According to the Foreign Investment Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from
January 1, 2020, the “Foreign Investment Law”), promulgated by the NPC on March 15, 2019, foreign
investment refers to investment activities carried out directly or indirectly within the territory of China by
foreign natural persons, enterprises, or other organizations (the foreign investors), including the following
situations: (1) a foreign investor establishing foreign-invested enterprises in China individually or jointly
with other investor; (2) a foreign investor acquiring shares, equity interests, property shares, or other
similar rights and interests in enterprises within the territory of China; (3) a foreign investor investing in
and establishing new projects in China individually or jointly with other investor; and (4) other forms of
investment as stipulated by laws, administrative regulations, or provisions of the State Council. The
Foreign Investment Law further implements the pre-establishment national treatment plus negative list
management system for foreign investment.
According to the Regulations for the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law of the People’s
Republic of China (effective from January 1, 2020), promulgated by the State Council , the state
encourages and promotes foreign investment, protects the legitimate rights and interests of foreign
investors, regulates the management of foreign investment, continuously optimizes the foreign investment
environment, and promotes a higher level of opening up.

Security Review of Foreign Investment
According to the National Security Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from July 1,
2015) and the Measures for the Security Review of Foreign Investment (effective from January 18, 2021),

Regulations Related to Cyber and Data Security
Network Security
According to the Cybersecurity Law of the People’s Republic of China (the “PRC Cybersecurity
Law,”) (effective from June 1, 2017), promulgated by the NPCSC , those which build or operate networks
or provide services through networks shall take technical measures and other necessary measures in
accordance with laws, administrative regulations and compulsory national requirements to safeguard the
safe and stable operation of the networks, respond to network security incidents effectively, prevent illegal
and criminal activities committed on the network, and maintain the integrity, confidentiality and
availability of network data.
The NPCSC issued the Decision on Amending the PRC Cybersecurity Law,
which took effect on January 1, 2026.
According to the Regulations on Network Data Security Management (effective from January 1,
2025), promulgated by the State Council , the Regulations on Network Data Security Management provides
detailed guidance on current regulatory requirements for various aspects of data processing, including the
disclosure of data processing rules by processors, the obtaining of general and separate consents, the
protection and security of important data, cross-border data transfers, and additional obligations imposed
on platform operators.
Data Security
According to the Data Security Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from September 1,
2021), promulgated by the NPCSC
, the state establishes a data classification and graded protection system,
implementing data classification and graded protection based on factors such as the importance of data in
economic and social development. When conducting data processing activities, entities shall, in
accordance with laws and regulations, establish and improve a full-process data security management
system, organize data security education and training, and adopt corresponding technical measures and
other necessary measures to ensure data security.

Regulations Related to Intellectual Property
Patents
According to the Patent Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from June 1, 2021),
promulgated by the NPCSC
, and the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People’s Republic
of China (effective from January 20, 2024), promulgated by the State Council , and relevant regulations,
patents are divided into 3 categories, i.e. invention patents, utility model patents and design patents. The
validity period of patents for inventions is 20 years, while the validity period of patents for utility models
is 10 years, and the validity period of patents for designs is 15 years (applications filed on or after 1 June
2021) or 10 years (applications filed on or before 31 May 2021), all starting from the date of application.
Trademarks
According to the Trademark Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from November 1,
2019), promulgated by the NPCSC
, as well as the Implementation Regulation of the PRC Trademark Law,
promulgated by the State Council , trademark registrants shall enjoy the right to exclusive use of their
trademarks and shall be protected by law. The validity period of a registered trademark is 10 years,
calculated from the date of approval for registration.
Copyrights
According to the Copyright Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from June 1, 2021),
promulgated by the NPCSC , and the Detailed Regulations on the Implementation of the Copyright Law
of the People’s Republic of China (effective from March 1, 2013), promulgated by the State Council ,
copyright owners enjoy various personal rights and property rights, including the right of publication, the
right of authorship, the right of reproduction, and the right of information network dissemination.

According to the Regulations on the Protection of Computer Software (effective from March 1,

Chinese citizens, legal persons, or other organizations shall enjoy copyrights for the software they

, the Integrated circuit layout design means the

According to the Law of the People’s Republic of China on the Administration of the Urban Real

, in the leasing of a house, the leaser

of the lease, liability for repair, as well as other rights and obligations of both parties, and shall register
the leasing with the department of housing administration for the record.
According to the Administrative Measures for Commodity House Leasing (effective from February

, the lessor and the lessee
are required to complete property leasing registration and filing formalities within 30 days from execution

such procedures, a fine ranging from RMB1,000 to RMB10,000 may be imposed on each lease agreement.
Additionally, according to the Regulation on Residential Property Leasing promulgated by the State
Council
(effective from September 15, 2025), lessors and lessees shall sign housing lease contracts using
their real names. Lessors shall file the housing lease contract with the real estate management department
in accordance with regulations; if the lessor fails to do so, the lessee may file the contract.

Regulations Related to Product Quality
According to the Product Quality Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from December
29, 2018), promulgated by the NPCSC , the manufacturers and sellers shall establish and perfect their
internal management of product quality, strictly implement quality criteria for various posts, specify
quality liabilities, and make checks accordingly. It is prohibited to forge or falsely use product quality
marks such as authentication marks. It is prohibited to forge the origin of products, to forge or falsely use
other’s factory name or address. It is prohibited to adulterate, to pass a fake product off as a genuine one,
or to pass a defective product off as a high quality one.
Regulations Related to Import and Export
According to the Foreign Trade Law of the People’s Republic of China and the Customs Law of the
People’s Republic of China, both promulgated by the NPCSC, the state generally permits the free import
and export of goods, technologies, and services, except as otherwise stipulated. The Customs of the PRC
supervises import and export activities at the border. Pursuant to the Regulations of the People’s Republic
of China on Customs Declaration Entity Registration Management (effective from January 1, 2022)
promulgated by the General Administration of Customs, consignees and consignors of imported and
exported goods, as well as customs declaration enterprises, must obtain market entity qualifications and
complete customs record-filing procedures when going through customs declaration formalities.
According to the Notice on Matters Concerning the Registration of Consignors and Consignees of
Import and Export Goods issued by the Enterprise Management and Audit Department of the General
Administration of Customs on January 3, 2023, entities applying for registration as consignors or
consignees of import and export goods must obtain market entity qualification but are no longer required
to obtain foreign trade operator registration.

through registration procedures in accordance with the regulations of the foreign exchange administrative
department of the State Council. Where
approval or filing is required from relevant competent authorities,
such approval or filing shall be completed before foreign exchange registration.
According to the Provisions on Foreign Exchange Administration of Foreign Investors’ Direct
Investment in China (effective from December 30, 2019), promulgated by the SAFE , the administration
of direct investment in China by foreign investors by SAFE or its local branches must be conducted
through registration, and banks must handle foreign exchange business related to direct investment in

Regulations Related to Labor and Employment
Labor Law and Labor Contract Law
According to the Labor Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from December 29, 2018),
promulgated by the NPCSC
and the PRC Labor Contract Law of the People’s Republic of China (the
“Labor Contract Law”) (effective from July 1, 2013), promulgated by the NPCSC , employers and workers
shall sign written labor contracts when establishing labor relations. Wages shall not be lower than the local
minimum wage standards. Employers shall establish and improve labor rules and regulations in
accordance with the law to ensure that workers enjoy labor rights and fulfill labor obligations.
Social Insurance and Housing Provident Funds
According to the Social Insurance Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from December
29, 2018), promulgated by the NPCSC
, and the Provisional Regulations on Collection and Payment of
Social Insurance Premiums (effective from March 24, 2019), promulgated by the State Council , a social
insurance system consisting of a basic pension insurance, basic medical insurance, work injury insurance,
unemployment insurance, and maternity insurance has been established. An employer shall, within thirty
days from the date of incorporation of the entity, proceed with the business license, registration certificate
or entity seal to the local social insurance agency to apply for social insurance registration. An employer
shall, within thirty days after taking on labor, proceed to the social insurance agency to apply for social
insurance registrations on behalf of the employees.
On July 31, 2025, the PRC Supreme People’s Court promulgated the Interpretation (II) on Several
Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Labor Dispute Cases, effective September 1, 2025. The
Judicial Interpretation stipulates that if an employer and an employee agree or the employee undertakes
to waive social insurance contributions, the People’s Court shall deem such agreement or undertaking
invalid. Furthermore, where an employer fails to pay social insurance contributions in accordance with the
law and the employee seeks to terminate the labour contract and claims economic compensation pursuant
to Article 38(3) of the PRC Labor Contract Law, the People’s Court shall support such claims. This
clarifies that employees are entitled to terminate their labour contracts and receive corresponding
economic compensation under the PRC Labor Contract Law if the employer fails to make social insurance
contributions in accordance with the law.
