Regulations Related to Taxation
Enterprise Income Tax
According to the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from
December 29, 2018, the “EIT Law”), promulgated by the NPC
, and the Regulations on the Implementation
of the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China (effective from January 20, 2025, the
Regulations on the Implementation of the EIT Law), promulgated by the State Council
, domestic
enterprises established in accordance with the law within the territory of China or established in
accordance with the laws of foreign countries (regions) but with their actual management entities within
the territory of China are deemed as resident enterprises. Resident enterprises shall pay enterprise income
tax at a rate of 25% on any income generated within or outside the territory of China. High-tech enterprises
supported by the state may pay enterprise income tax at a reduced rate of 15%. Qualified small enterprises
earning low profits may pay enterprise income tax at a reduced rate of 20%.
V alue-added Tax
Pursuant to the V alue-added Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China, which came into effect on
January 1, 2026, and the Regulations for the Implementation of the V alue-added Tax Law of the People’s
Republic of China, which came into effect on the same day, entities and individuals (including individual
businesses) engaged in the sale of goods, provision of services, transfer of intangible assets and
immovables, and importation of goods within the territory of China are VAT taxpayers. The sale of goods,
provision of services, transfer of intangible assets and sale of immovables shall mean the compensated
transfer of ownership of goods and immovables, the provision of services for compensation, and the
compensated transfer of the ownership or use right of intangible assets.

, as well as the Notice on the Arrangement for the Administration of Overseas

domestic enterprises that directly or indirectly issue securities overseas or list their securities for trading

INTERNATIONAL SANCTIONS LA WS AND REGULATIONS
U.S.
OFAC is the primary agency responsible for administering U.S. sanctions programmes against
targeted countries, entities, and individuals. “Primary” U.S. sanctions apply to “U.S. persons” or activities
involving a U.S. nexus (e.g., funds transfers in U.S. currency even if performed by non-U.S. persons), and
“secondary” U.S. sanctions apply extraterritorially to the activities of non-U.S. persons even when the
transaction has no U.S. nexus. Generally, U.S. persons are defined as entities organized under U.S. law
(such as companies and their U.S. subsidiaries); any U.S. entity’s domestic and foreign branches
(sanctions against Iran and Cuba also apply to U.S. companies’ foreign subsidiaries or other non-U.S.
entities owned or controlled by U.S. persons); U.S. citizens or permanent resident aliens (“green card”
holders), regardless of their location in the world; individuals physically present in the United States; and
U.S. branches or U.S. subsidiaries of non-U.S. companies.
Depending on the sanctions program and/or parties involved, U.S. law also may require a U.S.
company or a U.S. person to “block” (freeze) any assets/property interests owned, controlled or held for
the benefit of a sanctioned country, entity, or individual when such assets/property interests are in the
United States or within the possession or control of a U.S. person. Upon such blocking, no transaction may
be undertaken or effected with respect to the asset/property interest except pursuant to an authorization or
license from OFAC.
OFAC also prohibits virtually all business dealings with persons and entities identified in the SDN
List. Entities that a party on the SDN List owns (defined as a direct or indirect ownership interest of 50%
or more, individually or in the aggregate) are also blocked, regardless of whether that entity is expressly
named on the SDN List.

Other jurisdictions
The United Nations Security Council (the “ UNSC ”) can take action to maintain or restore
international peace and security under Chapter VII of the United Nations Charter. Sanctions measures
encompass a broad range of enforcement options that do not involve the use of armed force. Since 1966,
the UNSC has established 30 sanctions regimes.The UNSC measures have ranged from comprehensive
economic and trade sanctions to more targeted measures such as arms embargoes, travel bans, and
financial or commodity restrictions.
Under European Union sanction measures, there is no “blanket” ban on doing business in or with a
jurisdiction targeted by sanctions measures. It is not generally prohibited or otherwise restricted for a
person or entity to do business with a counterparty in a country subject to European Union sanctions where
that counterparty is not a Sanctioned Person and not engaged in prohibited activities provided that no
funds and economic resources are made available to the Sanctioned Persons.
As of January 1, 2021, the United Kingdom is no longer an EU member state. EU law including EU
sanctions measures continued to apply to and in the United Kingdom until December 31, 2020. EU
sanctions measures had also been extended by the United Kingdom on a regime by regime basis to apply
in the United Kingdom overseas territories, including the Cayman Islands. Starting from January 1, 2021,
the United Kingdom applies its own sanctions programs and has extended its autonomous sanctions
regimes to apply to and in the United Kingdom overseas territories.
The Australian restrictions and prohibitions arising from the sanctions laws apply broadly to any
person in Australia, any Australian anywhere in the world, companies incorporated overseas that are
owned or controlled by Australians or persons in Australia .

OVERVIEW
Our history can be traced back to 2018 when we were established as a limited liability company in
the PRC. After years of development, we have become a leading domestic provider of high-performance
automotive-grade SoCs, delivering comprehensive automotive intelligence solutions that power key
intelligent vehicle functions, from intelligent cockpit to mid-to-high-level advanced driver assistance.
MILESTONES

subsequently set up in Beijing and Shanghai.

Strategic benefits of Pre-IPO Investments
At the time of the Pre-IPO Investments, our Directors were of the view that the Pre-IPO Investors
would provide not only additional capital but also strategic resources that would support the long-term
development of our Group. The Pre-IPO Investments also demonstrated the Pre-IPO Investors’ confidence
in our business fundamentals and growth prospects. Leveraging the capabilities and industry networks of
the Pre-IPO Investors, we have been able to identify and capture new business opportunities. In particular:

including the R&D of core technologies, expansion of mass production capabilities and advancement of
our global market presence, and enabled us to benefit from the Pre-IPO Investors’ extensive industry

(ii) the participation of reputable Pre-IPO

(iv) the participation of global institutional investors

PUBLIC FLOAT AND FREE FLOAT
Satisfaction of the Public Float Requirement
The minimum prescribed percentage of H Shares held by public at the time of Listing pursuant to
Rule 19A.13A(1) of the Listing Rules would be the higher of (i) the percentage that would result in the
expected market value of H Shares held by the public to be HK$1,500,000,000 at the time of Listing; and
(ii) 15%. Assuming an Offer Price of HK$[
48.00], HK$[5 0.00] and HK$[5 2.00] per Offer Share (being the
low-end, mid-end and the high-end of the Offer Price, respectively), the percentage that would result in
the expected market value of H Shares held by the public to be HK$1,500,000,000 at the time of Listing
is approximately [9. 61]%, [9.22]% and [8.8 7]%, being less than 15%. Therefore, the minimum prescribed
percentage of H Shares held by public at the time of Listing pursuant to Rule 19A.13A(1) of the Listing
Rules of the Company is 15%.
Immediately upon completion of the Global Offering (assuming the Conversion of Unlisted Shares
into H Shares is completed and the Over-allotment Option is not exercised), our Company will have
[
325,329,516] Shares in total, all of which are H Shares. Among these [325,329,516] Shares:
(1) among the [ 276,530,116] H Shares:
a. the [ 127,346,567] H Shares held by M&M, Jingkai Entities and Share Incentive Platforms
to be converted from Unlisted Shares pursuant to the Conversion of Unlisted Shares into
H Shares of the Company and Listing on the Stock Exchange (representing approximately
[
39.14]% of our total issued Shares upon Listing) will not be counted towards the public
float for the purpose of Rule 19A.13A(1) of the Listing Rules after the Listing as such
Shares are held by our core connected persons of our Company or their respective close
associates;
b. the [
149,183,549] H Shares to be converted from Unlisted Shares pursuant to the
Conversion of Unlisted Shares into H Shares and Listing on the Stock Exchange
(representing approximately [ 45.86]% of our total issued Shares upon Listing) will be
counted towards the public float for the purpose of Rule 19A.13A(1) of the Listing Rules.
These H Shares are held by our Pre-IPO Investors and existing shareholders other than
M&M, Jingkai Entities and Share Incentive Platforms and these shareholders will not be
core connected persons of our Company upon Listing nor are they accustomed to take
instructions from

not financed directly or indirectly by
our Company’s core connected persons; and
(2) [ 48,799,400] H Shares will be issued pursuant to the Listing.
In light of the above, immediately following the completion of the Global Offering, the total number
of H Shares expected to be held by the public represents approximately [ 60.86]% of the total issued share
capital of our Company, thereby satisfying the public float requirement under Rule 19A.13A(1) of the
Listing Rules.
Satisfaction of the Free Float Requirement
Rule 19A.13C(1) of the Listing Rules provides that, where a new applicant is a PRC issuer with no
other listed shares at the time of listing, this will normally mean that the portion of H shares for which
listing is sought that are held by the public and not subject to any disposal restrictions (whether under
contract, the Listing Rules, applicable laws or otherwise), at the time of listing, must: (a) represent at least
10% of the total number of issued shares in the class to which H shares belong at the time of listing
(excluding treasury shares), with an expected market value at the time of listing of not less than
HK$50,000,000; or (b) have an expected market value at the time of listing of not less than
HK$600,000,000.

OVERVIEW
Who We Are
We are a leading domestic provider of high-performance automotive-grade SoCs, delivering
comprehensive automotive intelligence solutions that power key intelligent vehicle functions, from
intelligent cockpit to mid- to high-level advanced driver assistance. Our strategic focus lies in the design
and development of advanced automotive-grade SoCs and solutions.
We have focused on AI-powered
cockpits and the integration of cockpit and driving functionalities. We are the No. 1 domestic supplier in
the automotive SoC market in China in 2025, in terms of installation volume of intelligent cockpit domain
controller SoCs, according to Frost & Sullivan. Leveraging our system-level design approach enabling
unified chip architecture, foundational software platform and comprehensive ecosystem support, we
deliver high-performance automotive-grade SoCs
without compromising on cost or efficiency. Our
SoC-based solutions are built on proprietary automotive-grade SoCs, empowered by foundational software
platform. Through in-house technological innovation and close collaboration with automotive OEMs and
tier-one suppliers, we continuously refine our products and drive their adoption across major automotive
platforms.
The global automotive industry is undergoing a fundamental transition toward digital and AI-driven
intelligent cockpits, centralized electrical and electronic (“ E/E”) architectures and ADAS powered by
multi-modal perception and large AI models. As vehicle intelligence accelerates, demand for high-
performance automotive-grade SoCs is
expanding, and SoCs will become the core computing engine
defining next-generation vehicle experience and competitiveness. At the same time, industrial intelligence
is shifting computation from cloud to edge, where low-latency, secure and power-efficient AI processing
is essential. This trend makes heterogeneous high-integration SoCs the foundational compute platform for
emerging robotics and edge AI applications. SiEngine was born out of the firm belief in this industry-wide
transformation. Our core team is composed of veterans from leading global semiconductor companies
with
expertise in advanced computing chips across automotive, server, and high-performance computing
applications. Leveraging this experience, they anticipated the growing demand for high-performance chips
in the automotive sector driven by the rise of intelligent vehicles. Since our inception, we have focused
on developing
automotive-grade SoCs using the latest processing techniques, such as the advanced 7nm
process, to deliver compute capacity, energy efficiency and integration density. Recognizing that the
stringent requirements applicable to automotive-grade applications are similarly critical in industrial
automation and edge computing scenarios, we have strategically extended the application of our
automotive-grade SoCs to these adjacent high-growth markets. Leveraging a unified architecture and
reusable modules, we are able to efficiently adapt our solutions to meet the reliability, performance and
environmental demands of industrial deployments. This forward-looking strategy has enabled us to
penetrate the market with a scalable, reusable product portfolio.
In 2021, we launched SE1000, China’s first 7nm automotive-grade intelligent cockpit SoC. Since the

controller SoCs. In 202 5, the shipment volume of SE1000 reached 839,000 units, with cumulative shipments

Industry Pain Points and Our Value Propositions
As automotive intelligence and software-defined vehicle transformation accelerate, automotive
OEMs face three structural challenges: rapid growth in demand for automotive-grade high-performance
computing, the widening gap between fast-iterating AI capabilities and long vehicle lifecycles, and the
need for multi-domain functional integration with a single chip that drives up the total implementation
cost. These pressures require solutions that deliver sustained performance scalability, long-term AI
upgradability and system-level cost efficiency.
 Surging demand for automotive-grade high-performance computing : The automotive
industry is experiencing explosive demand for intelligent features like advanced driver-
assistance systems (“ ADAS ”) and intelligent and AI-powered cockpits, which are rapidly
shifting from premium options to standard configurations across all vehicle segments. This
demand is driven not only by growing consumer expectations for smarter and safer vehicles but
also by automotive OEMs’ increasing focus on mitigating supply chain risks. To ensure
flexibility in product planning and avoid over-reliance on a limited number of suppliers,
automotive OEMs are actively seeking more qualified and diversified solution providers. These
trends have significantly increased the need for high-performance, automotive-grade SoCs with
advanced AI capabilities, low latency, functional safety, and the scalability to support both
consumer demands and automotive OEM strategies.
 Mismatch between rapid AI evolution and long vehicle lifecycles : AI capabilities are
advancing at unprecedented speed, with algorithms and foundational models iterating every
one to two years, while automotive products operate on 10- to 15-year lifecycles and demand
long-term reliability and functional continuity. As vehicle launch cycles accelerate and model
refresh frequencies shorten, automotive OEMs are under increasing pressure to support
continuous feature expansion and AI upgrades from the moment a vehicle enters production.
Without scalable compute headroom and reconfigurable AI capability, vehicles risk becoming
obsolete within three to five years, undermining consumer experience and brand
competitiveness. To bridge this structural gap, automotive OEMs require open, extensible and
programmable SoC platforms rather than closed turnkey solutions, enabling sustained
evolution across the entire vehicle lifecycle.

 Rising importance of total implementation cost : As intelligent functions are integrated into
mass-market vehicles, automotive system architectures are growing more complex. This shift
requires automotive OEMs to place greater emphasis on total implementation cost rather than
standalone chip pricing. Without efficient and open toolchains, developers struggle to fully
utilize low-level compute resources. Insufficient hardware-software integration drives up
system integration time and effort. Additionally, weak platform scalability limits cross-model
reuse, increasing bill of materials (“ BOM”) and long-term maintenance costs. These challenges
have pushed automotive OEMs to demand higher on-chip functional integration and cost-
optimized co-design across peripheral components, system devices and hardware-software
decoupling, making single-chip fusion of major computing domains the most critical path to
cost reduction. As a result, the architectural complexity of high-performance automotive SoCs
has reached an unprecedented level, requiring fundamentally different design and development
approaches.
Since our inception, we have been committed to systematically addressing these fundamental
challenges:
 Reliable high-performance SoC offerings : Reliable automotive-grade SoCs are the foundation
of intelligent cockpit or ADAS solutions. Leveraging our
expertise in high-performance chip
design, we have from the outset committed ourselves to adopting an automotive-grade
technology roadmap, utilizing advanced process nodes and heterogeneous multi-core
architecture, and prioritizing rigorous safety, reliability, and quality standards to meet the
demanding requirements of next-generation intelligent vehicles.
 System-level design and open ecosystem : We approach every aspect of SoC and solution
design and development with a
system-level mindset. By integrating hardware innovation, a
foundational software platform and an open ecosystem, we simplify system integration and
reduce engineering, validation and lifecycle expenses across vehicle platforms. Our open and
scalable compute foundation enables automotive OEMs, algorithm developer and application
developer to build and iterate solutions on our platform instead of relying on closed turnkey
systems with limited extensibility. This system-level design methodology will accelerate
development cycles, time-to-market and deliver meaningful performance-cost advantages
across multiple vehicle models and generations, supporting predictable commercialization and
sustainable competitiveness for automotive OEMs.

Market alignment and customer-centric co-development : We define and architect our SoCs
through co-development with automotive OEMs from the earliest concept stage, aligning chip
definition with real engineering requirements and vehicle platform roadmaps, ensuring
synchronized evolution with technology trends. By embedding customer needs and application
scenarios directly into chip architecture and product planning, we build solutions that
accurately match market needs and enable strategically structured SoC portfolios. Further,
through close collaboration with strategic customers and synchronization with their
development timelines, together with self-developed architecture and optimized supply chain
management, we deliver high-performance, cost-competitive SoCs that support rapid and
predictable vehicle launches across multiple model series.

We have built a full-scenario portfolio of automotive-grade high-performance SoCs, based on which
we offer solutions covering applications from intelligent cockpit to ADAS.

Intelligent Cockpit SoCs
Our intelligent cockpit SoC portfolio spans a full range of scenarios from entry-level to premium
intelligent cockpits, and from integrated cockpit-driving-parking solutions to next-generation cockpit-
driving fusion.
Our flagship product, SE1000, is China’s first 7nm automotive-grade intelligent cockpit SoC,
breaking the long-standing dominance of international suppliers in this segment. Built on advanced 7nm
process technology, SE1000 delivers high computing power, high integration, low power consumption and
high-level security, benchmarking closely against global flagship peers. Having adopted a forward-looking
architecture with dedicated interfaces and functional modules for NPU integration, the standard version
of our SE1000 enables cockpit-driving-parking integration, representing the industry’s first high-value,
all-in-one cockpit-driving-parking solution. We have also launched a functionally trimmed version of
SE1000, namely our SE500, targeting basic intelligent cockpit applications. SE500 offers a cost-effective
solution for entry-level vehicle segments while maintaining the core capabilities of our flagship
architecture, enabling us to address the diverse performance and cost requirements from entry-level to
premium vehicle segments.
SE2000 is our next-generation intelligent cockpit SoC, which is expected to
rival international
cockpit chips, enabling both AI-powered intelligent cockpit experiences and seamless cockpit-driving
fusion. Manufactured using a 5nm automotive-grade process node, SE2000 is designed for multi-modal
interaction and edge AI inference, and delivers improved computing performance compared to our
current-generation products. SE2000 features next-generation advanced NPU and GPU, enabling rich
in-cabin visual experiences and advanced AI acceleration.
ADAS SoCs
Our ADAS SoC portfolio is designed to support a comprehensive range of assisted driving scenarios,
from L2 assisted driving to highway and urban Navigate on Autopilot (“ NOA”), full-scenario autonomous
driving, and advanced cockpit-driving fusion.
AD1000 is a high-performance automotive-grade SoC built on 7nm process technology and a
heterogeneous multi-core architecture that delivers
computation capacity with native LLM support.
AD1000 delivers NPU performance of 512 TOPS, and can be scaled up to 2,048 TOPS via multi-chip
cascading. AD1000 is positioned to provide the core computing foundation for the widespread adoption
of advanced autonomous driving capabilities, including urban NOA.
AD2000 is envisioned as the cerebral brain of future intelligent vehicles, delivering higher
computing capabilities and enhanced integration of compute and storage resources to lay the technical
groundwork for L3, L4 and higher levels of autonomous driving.
AI Accelerator SoCs
Our NNA100 is an edge AI chip simultaneously meeting automotive-grade requirements and
functional safety standards, which expects to obtain AEC-Q100 Grade 3 qualification and ISO 26262
ASIL-B certification.

Our
System-Level Architecture and Design
We adopt a system-level architecture and design approach that begins with analyzing the
requirements and specifications of evolving automotive E/E architectures and in-vehicle application
systems. We perform system-level modeling, simulation and validation to define a complete architectural
blueprint before allocating responsibilities across the chip, software and ecosystem layers through a
coordinated hardware-software co-design methodology. This full-stack process integrates SoC design,
foundational software platforms and ecosystem enablement into a unified development flow. It enables
high performance and reliability while delivering significant gains in system efficiency, flexibility and
scalability, ensuring effective implementation and rapid iteration in complex automotive environments.
Foundational Layer: Advanced SoC Chip Design

cockpit series and ADAS series to our AI accelerator series, developed under a unified, high-performance
architecture independently designed by us. Leveraging advanced process technologies and
expertise in
SoC architecture, we enable configurable and scalable heterogeneous multi-core resources, high compute
throughput and low latency within stringent automotive power and thermal constraints. The architecture
incorporates
reliability and functional safety mechanisms that ensure isolation across processing domains
and system resilience in complex vehicle environments. By anticipating system-level software

that support efficient upper-layer software integration and broad application adaptability. This foundation
allows us to
build differentiated product portfolios and provide high-performance, high-bandwidth,
high-security and power-efficient computing platforms for next-generation intelligent vehicles.

Intermediate Layer: Foundational Software Platform
Our foundational software platform serves as the critical technical bridge between hardware and
applications, comprising multi-OS integration, board support package (“ BSP”) and a suite of development
tools, ensuring seamless integration and an efficient fit for diverse customer needs. Built on our
heterogeneous multi-core SoC architecture, the software platform enables integration and coordinated
support for multiple operating environments, including Linux, Android and RTOS, and efficient workload
execution within the most suitable system context. It incorporates a rigorously validated BSP that provides
essential low-level drivers and firmware, comprehensive middleware that streamlines complex system
functions such as multimedia processing, graphics rendering, data sharing and communication protocols,
and toolchains that support build compilation, debugging, performance profiling, image construction and
package management. In addition,
ready-to-use templates for typical automotive scenarios offer sample
software that accelerate customer development. This comprehensive software platform establishes a solid
foundation for ecosystem expansion and enables efficient development and deployment across diverse
vehicle platforms.
Top Layer: Comprehensive Ecosystem Support
For automotive-grade SoCs, close alignment between hardware and software is critical. Built on top
of our SoCs and foundational software platform, our comprehensive and open ecosystem facilitates
hardware-software compatibility across automotive use cases and enables automotive OEMs, tier-one
suppliers and application developers to
deploy and scale our products, accelerating time-to-market. We
collaborate extensively with peripheral hardware and module supplier and tier-one partners to broaden
hardware compatibility for our SoCs. We also work with commercial OS provider, algorithm developer,
application developer and solution integrator to establish a complete software ecosystem. In addition, we
provide hardware and software development platforms, reference designs, debugging tools and technical
collaboration channels, enabling developers to experiment, optimize and commercialize applications more
efficiently. This open environment offers customers greater flexibility and choice while reducing
integration complexity and deployment cost.

controls, and integrity verification. This security architecture aligns with emerging automotive

autonomous vehicles.

integrated approach allows us to deliver not just a chip, but a comprehensive platform that lowers
customers’ total implementation costs and accelerates their time-to-market:
 Unified core architecture with high integration : We develop all our SoCs, spanning intelligent
cockpit, ADAS and AI accelerator, under a unified, high-performance architecture
independently designed by us. This unified architecture enables scalable and consistent
heterogeneous computing across product lines, supporting rapid feature expansion and efficient
IP module reuse to meet diverse vehicle system requirements. Our SoCs achieve high levels of
functional integration by coordinating multiple heterogeneous compute units, including CPU,
GPU, NPU, DSP , MCU and in-house IP , to efficiently support different data processing flows
across cockpit, perception and AI workloads within a single chip. Built on advanced process
technologies, this architecture delivers high compute density, low latency and
power efficiency
while reducing overall system cost and component count. By further integrating hardware-level
isolation mechanisms, including secure processing islands and resource partitioning, we enable
domain separation and functional safety. This allows complex vehicle computing scenarios to
run concurrently with enhanced resilience. This approach forms a scalable and efficient
computing foundation for next-generation intelligent vehicles.
 Foundational software platform : We have developed a foundational software platform that
serves as the system-level bridge between our SoCs and upper-layer applications. The platform
provides a full-stack, comprehensive solution, including multi OS integration, BSP
and a suite
of development tools. It comprehensively supports diverse development needs for intelligent
cockpit and ADAS systems and is designed to significantly enhance software development
efficiency, reduce system integration complexity, and enable shorter time-to-market for
customers. At the core of the platform is our proprietary unified software architecture, which
supports intelligent cockpit, autonomous driving, cockpit-driving- parking integrations and
cockpit-driving fusion in a general computing framework. By delivering this unified,
production-proven software platform alongside our SoCs, we enable automotive OEMs and
tier-one suppliers to reduce engineering complexity, improve delivery predictability, and focus
on innovation at the application layer.
 Comprehensive ecosystem support : Built on top of our SoCs and foundational software
platform, our comprehensive and open ecosystem support enables automotive OEMs, tier-one
suppliers and application developers to
deploy and scale our products, accelerating time-to-
market. We collaborate extensively with memory, power management, sensor, and connectivity
component vendors, as well as peripheral hardware and module supplier and tier-one partners,
to expand hardware compatibility, ensuring that our SoCs can be directly integrated with
mainstream peripheral components and vehicle platforms with reduced engineering effort. We
also work closely with commercial OS provider, algorithm developer, application developer
and solution integrator to build a complete software ecosystem that supports voice interaction,
multi-modal AI, perception processing and user experience applications. In addition, we
provide hardware and software development platforms, reference designs, debugging tools and
technical collaboration channels, enabling developers to experiment, optimize and
commercialize applications more efficiently. This open environment offers customers great
flexibility and choice while reducing integration complexity and deployment cost.

and reliability testing before it can enter mass production. As a result, there is typically a time lag between product
launch and mass production.

conditions are met, we will further consider customer and market demands in determining whether to proceed with

Intelligent Cockpit SoCs and Solutions
To address the increasing performance and functional demands of automotive-grade cockpit systems,
we developed our proprietary StarEagle series of intelligent cockpit SoCs for next-generation intelligent
vehicles. Built on the 7nm and more advanced process node and a scalable heterogeneous computing
architecture, the StarEagle series delivers strong computing performance, bandwidth, low latency and
multi-OS support, while also aligning with industry trends such as cockpit-driving-parking integration and
AI-powered intelligent cabins. According to Frost & Sullivan, SE1000, the first product in our StarEagle
series, achieved multiple industry firsts in China’s automotive-grade SoC market, including the first
domestically mass-produced 7nm automotive-grade intelligent cockpit SoC and the first mass-produced
single-chip solution integrating cockpit, driving and parking functions. We were the No. 1 domestic
supplier in the automotive SoC market in China in 2025, in terms of installation volume of intelligent
cockpit domain controller SoCs, with a market share of 5.6%.
To meet the demands of automotive-grade intelligent cockpits for high computing power, bandwidth,
low latency, multi-OS support, and diverse user scenarios, as well as emerging trends in integrated systems
and AI applications, we have developed our intelligent cockpit solutions
based on our intelligent cockpit
SoCs. Building on our SoC’s hardware partitioning and heterogeneous multi-core architecture, our

, and different computing units can run tasks in their

 Heterogeneous multi-core architecture : Our StarEagle series is built on a heterogeneous
multi-core architecture to efficiently handle the diverse workloads of modern intelligent
cockpits. We have pioneered a hardware-level partition between CPU and GPU, with other
computing units flexibly configured based on vehicle needs. This design eliminates reliance on
traditional virtualization software, significantly improving CPU and GPU efficiency and
enabling faster, smoother applications while reducing system costs. Each module is optimized
for a specific class of tasks
:
/H11568CPU is responsible for general-purpose processing, operating system management, and
control logic execution, and enables seamless switching across multi-OS environments
and real-time system response.
/H11568GPU handles graphical rendering tasks such as multi-screen display, UI animations, and
3D visualization, and delivers smooth user experiences even under heavy graphical
workloads.
/H11568NPU accelerates AI inference tasks such as voice recognition, visual perception, and user
behavior modeling. Our current-generation NPU achieves 8 TOPS (INT8), providing
sufficient compute power for multi-modal interaction.
/H11568DPU is optimized for display pipeline processing, including composition, scaling, and
timing control, across multiple screens.
/H11568ISP processes image input from cameras to support in-cabin vision applications, such as
driver monitoring and occupant identification, as well as image-preprocessing for
surround-view and DVR systems.
/H11568Audio DSP enables high-fidelity multi-channel audio playback and real-time acoustic
signal processing, supporting enhanced voice interaction and spatial sound.
/H11568Video Codec/Security Engine/Safety Island/Memory Subsystem together ensure high-
throughput video encoding/decoding, trust execution environments, functional safety
compliance (ASIL), and low-latency memory access.
By leveraging this modular and heterogeneous architecture, our StarEagle series
maintains
power and thermal efficiency critical for automotive-grade deployment. The architecture also
supports scalable feature configurations, allowing automotive OEMs to tailor compute
resources based on vehicle class and target market, while lowering manufacturing and supply
chain management costs through reduced BOM cost, PCB footprint, and overall system
complexity.
 High reliability and safety :
Our current intelligent cockpit SoC offerings have passed
AEC-Q100 reliability tests and obtained up to ASIL-D certification. It incorporates a
self-developed cryptographic engine compliant with national encryption standards and an
independent ASIL-D safety island to safeguard overall system security and safety.
Leveraging the scalability of the StarEagle platform, our intelligent cockpit product portfolio is
structured into three distinct tiers to address diverse market needs based on user experience and
automation levels. The entry-level tier, represented by SE500, focuses on essential digital displays and
basic safety functions for cost-sensitive vehicle segments. The standard tier, powered by our flagship
SE1000, provides immersive multi-screen cockpits with integrated parking assistance. The high-
performance tier, enabled by SE1000 combined with our AI accelerator, NNA100, unlocks advanced AI
capabilities, supporting complex tasks such as highway autopilot and generative AI interactions.

SE1000
Our flagship SE1000 was first introduced in December 2021 and commenced mass production in
March 2023, representing the earliest domestically-developed 7nm automotive-grade SoCs to reach
mass-market deployment.
Technical Advancement and Key Functionalities
SE1000 is fabricated using a 7nm automotive-grade process and meets the AEC-Q100 Grade 3
reliability standard, and is designed in compliance with ISO 26262 ASIL-B functional safety requirements.
SE1000 integrates the following key components: (i) an octa-core CPU, delivering computing
performance of up to 100 KDMIPS; (ii) a 14-core GPU with computing power of 900 GFLOPS; (iii) a
high-performance NPU offering 8 TOPS for real-time AI applications; (iv) LPDDR5 memory with up to
51.2 GB/s bandwidth; (v) an on-chip safety subsystem compliant with ISO 26262 ASIL-D; and (vi) a
self-developed encryption engine capable of supporting both national cryptographic algorithms and
international standards, offering server-grade data security for automotive applications. SE1000 delivers
the following performance highlights:
 Comprehensive cockpit functions : SE1000 supports multiple high-definition displays across
instrument cluster, central console, and passenger screens with seamless content display and
low-latency interaction. It supports multiple cameras for surround-view monitoring, driver and
occupant monitoring system, AI-powered vision processing for driver fatigue detection and
gesture control, immersive entertainment experiences with ultra-high-definition video
playback and 3D space audio, and intelligent voice interaction with advanced noise
cancellation technology.
 Integrated cockpit-driving-parking capability : As we adopted a forward-looking architecture
and reserved dedicated interfaces and functional modules for NPU integration, SE1000 enables
cockpit, driving assistance, and parking functions on a single chip, reducing total
implementation costs compared to traditional solutions requiring multiple chips, while
maintaining high performance. The integrated solution supports L2 ADAS functions including
intelligent cruise control (ICC), highway driving assistance (HDA), lane keeping assistance
(LKA), automatic lane changing (ALC), traffic sign recognition (TSR) and automatic
emergency braking (AEB), as well as advanced parking assistance (APA) systems capable of
addressing confined spaces and complex parking scenarios.
 High reliability and cost efficiency : SE1000 employs a hardware-based partition architecture
that enables safe concurrent operation of different vehicle functions on the same chip, allowing
previously separate control units to be consolidated into a single platform. This single-chip
integration approach reduces component costs, circuit board space requirements, and overall
system complexity while ensuring compliance with automotive functional safety standards. For
instance, by integrating functions that traditionally require external discrete components such
as display and audio processors, switch chips and MCU into a single SoC, SE1000 enables
estimated system BOM cost savings of approximately US$35 to US$45 per vehicle for
automotive OEMs and tier-one suppliers.

Targeted Scenarios
Building on our unified technology platform, SE1000 is offered in multiple product configurations
to flexibly address the varying performance, feature, and cost requirements of different vehicle classes.
These differentiated versions maintain core architectural consistency while enabling tailored compute
capability, I/O scalability, and peripheral integration suited to basic, mid-level, and advanced in-cabin use

The standard version of SE1000 targets mass-market passenger vehicles supporting intelligent
cockpit and integrated cockpit-driving-parking applications. SE1000 delivers comprehensive computing
capabilities tailored for advanced in-cabin use cases, representing our flagship solution for the
growing

tier-one suppliers to build (i) mid- to high-end intelligent cockpit systems, enabling AI-driven voice

and LPDDR bandwidth to reduce BOM cost, while maintaining essential cockpit functionalities. SE500
maintains full pin-to-pin compatibility with SE1000 and its accompanying software platform, enabling
faster customer development and validation.

ADAS SoCs and Solutions
Overview
Growing consumer demand for safer, more intelligent, and increasingly autonomous driving
experiences has accelerated the development of advanced driver assistance systems, driving
market
demand for high-performance ADAS SoCs. Our StarLight series targets ADAS applications,
benchmarking against leading international products. Built on a diverse heterogeneous multi-core
architecture, the StarLight series delivers high performance and low power consumption across full ADAS
scenarios. The design optimizes critical performance metrics including real-time processing, resource
allocation, and safety isolation. Through single-chip or multi-chip configurations, the series supports
computing requirements from L2+ to L4 autonomous driving.
Our ADAS solutions comprise a
software platform that includes stable low-level drivers, safety-
critical RTOS support, and modular middleware for perception, fusion, and control, all optimized for
real-time performance and functional safety through our specialized SDKs. To accelerate AI model
development and deployment, we provide a high-performance AI toolchain with
optimization for CNN and
transformer architectures. We also provide open SDKs and hardware abstraction layers that allow
customers to integrate their own algorithms and third-party modules, as well as fine-tune foundation
models. Our complete platform also offers multiple operating systems, BSP for chip and sensor
integration, ready-to-use AI algorithm libraries for autonomous driving scenarios, and reference
applications that showcase system functionalities enabled by our SoCs and provide customers with
implementable templates for their own deployments. Together, these capabilities enable tier-one suppliers
to accelerate algorithm deployment, system integration, and validation, supporting fast mass deployment
of advanced ADAS systems.
AD1000
AD1000, the first SoC in our StarLight series, was launched in March 2025, and became eligible for
mass production in December 2025. Built on a 7nm automotive-grade process and compliant with
AEC-Q100 Grade 3 and ISO 26262 ASIL-B standards, AD1000 is purpose-built for full-stack ADAS
deployment across L2+ to L4 scenarios, including urban NOA, highway NOA, and autonomous valet
parking (“ AV P”). It supports both single-chip deployment for L2+ and L4-A VP use cases and dual-chip
scalability for more compute-intensive L3+ functions, as well as highway and urban NOA, LLM
acceleration, AI inference acceleration and cockpit-driving fusion.
Technical Advancement and Performance Highlights
AD1000 features a heterogeneous multi-core architecture combining high-performance and high-
integration to address real-time processing demands across perception, planning, and control, integrating:
(i) CPU subsystem, delivering 250 KDMIPS; (ii) NPU with up to 512 TOPS (INT8) and large on-chip
SRAM for high-throughput AI inference with reduced memory bottlenecks; (iii) DSP unit offering 512
GFLOPS (FP32) to accelerate traditional signal processing workloads; and (iv) LPDDR5 memory with up
to 204 GB/s bandwidth. AD1000 delivers the following performance highlights:
 High computing power : AD1000 delivers over 250 KDMIPS of CPU performance and
incorporates a powerful NPU offering up to 512 TOPS at INT8 precision, with large on-chip
SRAM and a multi-level memory hierarchy that mitigates memory bottlenecks and
significantly enhances inference throughput and response time. In addition, its DSP achieves
up to 512 GFLOPS (FP32), and is
optimized for advanced perception models such as BEV
Transformer.

different versions to meet the diverse compute, sensor fusion and functional safety demands across ADAS

urban and highway NOA, and automatic/home parking assistance in mass-market and premium NEVs.

 L2+ system : The L2+ system supports highway and urban NOA, including automatic lane

high-definition maps, with configurations supporting lightweight LiDAR. We enable this

multi-core architecture enables efficient perception, fusion, and decision control, with
continuous OTA upgrade capability.

AI Accelerator SoCs
To address the limitation of most intelligent cockpit and ADAS SoCs of insufficient memory
bandwidth and inadequate AI computing power, which renders them incapable of efficiently supporting
large model inference, we have developed NNA100, our AI accelerator SoCs, designed to work alongside
in-vehicle SoCs. NNA100 aims to optimize large model performance in terms of both technical feasibility
and cost efficiency. We have completed the majority of the engineering-sample-stage development and
validation work, with remaining tasks proceeding as planned. We launched NNA100 in April 2025, which
will be eligible for mass production in June 2026.
NNA100 is an automotive-grade SoC built on a 7nm process and compliant with AEC-Q100 Grade
3 and ISO 26262 ASIL-B standards. These attributes ensure
adaptability to automotive and industrial
control environments, delivering a balanced combination of performance, safety, and reliability for
in-vehicle large model inference.
NNA100 delivers approximately CPU performance of 50 KDMIPS, while supporting up to 128-bit
LPDDR5 memory with a bandwidth up to 102.4 GB/s. Our AI accelerator SoCs are equipped with a
complete toolchain for AI development, debugging, and deployment, and are purpose-built for efficient
on-device LLM inference, VLMs, and ADAS models, enabling local LLM support and highway NOA.
NNA100 offers core optimizations for matrix multiplication, convolution, and Transformer operations,
and supports multiple precision formats, such as INT16, FP16, and BF16.

Industrial-Grade SoCs

TECHNOLOGY
Architecture Design
All of our SoCs are developed based on a unified proprietary architecture specifically engineered for
automotive applications. Safety-critical ADAS systems require real-time performance, while intelligent
cockpits need the flexibility to run feature-rich applications. Our architecture enables flexible allocation
of heterogeneous multi-core computing resources while maintaining the isolation and reliability that
automotive applications demand.
Hardware-Software Co-Design Approach
The architecture adopts an integrated hardware-software approach, combining software-level
coordination with hardware-level isolation to deliver high performance comparable to hardware-based
solutions, while maintaining software-level flexibility in implementation. Under this architecture,
computing resources and peripherals are allocated across different domains in accordance with customer
requirements. Symmetric processing within individual domains enables efficient multi-core
communication and data sharing, while asymmetric processing across domains supports secure isolation
between different workloads.
The on-chip interconnect system enables concurrent AI computing, high-resolution video processing,
and multiple camera and display support while maintaining functional independence and security across
different systems. During development, our design and software teams jointly define requirements and
specifications for key subsystems including resource allocation, communication paths, system boot
sequences, operating system scheduling, virtualization management, and cross-domain communication.
By implementing these capabilities directly into the unified architecture of our SoCs, we are able to
achieve design reuse and share engineering experience across different SoCs, thereby enabling more
efficient allocation of development resources. This approach enhances resource utilization, simplifies
design complexity, reduces post-design modification risks, and accelerates our overall development cycle.
Comprehensive Software Infrastructure
Beyond the SoC hardware platform, we provide a comprehensive software infrastructure that serves
as the critical bridge between hardware and applications. Built upon our SoC hardware partitioning and
heterogeneous multi-core architecture, our software platform employs advanced architectural principles to
achieve
integration and collaborative support for multiple operating systems including Linux, Android,
Micro-kernel, and RTOS environments.
Our full-stack software platform comprises (i) operating system layer, that enables different
computing units and domains to execute tasks efficiently within their most suitable operating system
environments ; (ii) BSPs covering low-level drivers, virtualization support, and firmware for all hardware
modules ; (iii) middleware component libraries that optimize complex functions, such as multimedia
processing, graphics rendering, data sharing and distribution, communication protocols, cross-domain
communication, and runtime management
; (iv) engineering toolchain spanning compilation and building,
model and operator compilation, debugging and performance profiling, image construction and package
management, and continuous integration
; and (v) reference applications that provide customers with

Chip Technologies
Unified Multi-Domain Architecture
Our architecture allows computing resources to be accurately allocated based on application needs.
Unlike traditional heterogeneous SoC designs, our architecture supports reallocation of computing
resources and peripherals according to different customer applications.
 Symmetric and asymmetric compatible architecture : Through dynamic grouping, we achieve
symmetric data-coherent processing within computing domains and asymmetric data
processing between domains. Symmetric processing enables efficient communication and data
sharing for multi-core computing, while asymmetric processing ensures secure isolation of
system data. This multi-domain architecture realizes the repartitioning of core computing
resources into symmetric and asymmetric domains, resolving the differences in computing
resource requirements across multiple domains for different customers.
 Domain isolation and integration : Within each computing domain, resources work together
efficiently for high-speed processing. Between domains,
isolation ensures failures in one
domain do not affect others. This flexibility lets customers configure the chip for different use
cases without relying entirely on software virtualization, which can introduce performance
overhead and complexity.
 Advanced interconnect technology : Our interconnect technology manages data flow between
chip subsystems. Based on coherent interconnect technology and on-chip network transmission
architecture, it supports dynamic priority configuration for data transmission, intelligent
bandwidth adjustment, and bandwidth monitoring. This interconnect technology is fundamental
to our multi-domain architecture support, achieving both high efficiency in data sharing and
data security. It accommodates different bandwidth performance and latency requirements of
various peripherals, supporting adaptive bandwidth adjustment to meet low-latency and
high-bandwidth needs of different peripheral interfaces at low cost.
High-Performance Processing
For vision-intensive applications like autonomous driving, processing multiple camera feeds in real
time is computationally demanding. Our approach combines architectural innovation with specialized
acceleration.
 Video and image processing optimization : Our chip architecture addresses high-bandwidth
video and image processing requirements through architectural innovation and dedicated
algorithm hardware acceleration optimization. In video and image processing pipeline
architecture design, we employ streaming processing architecture, cross-domain zero-copy
technology, and lossless bandwidth compression for video stream ingress and egress from
storage areas, reducing double data rate (“ DDR”) bandwidth consumption in these application
scenarios. For dedicated algorithm hardware acceleration, our optical flow and stereo vision
algorithm accelerators designed for autonomous driving scenarios achieve more efficient
algorithm acceleration compared to general-purpose processors.
 Memory architecture and bandwidth : To address the memory bandwidth bottleneck in AI
computing, our architecture employs a dual strategy. First, a hierarchical buffering system
keeps frequently accessed data close to the computing units, minimizing latency and off-chip
memory traffic. Second, our multi-level, grouped DDR interleaving transmission mode

Software Platform
Beyond chip hardware, we provide a comprehensive software platform including system software,
BSPs, middleware, engineering toolchains, and reference implementations. This integrated platform
accelerates customer time-to-market and enables rapid deployment across vehicle models.
Our software architecture separates different layers so they can update independently without
causing interruptions to the entire system. Operating systems, middleware, and applications can each be
updated or replaced without significantly affecting others. This modularity is essential given that
autonomous driving sensors need real-time response measured in milliseconds, intelligent cockpit
applications need rich application ecosystems, and safety-critical functions need guaranteed isolation from
potential failures in feature-rich software. We support multiple operating systems running concurrently,
with communication mechanisms enabling efficient and secure data sharing across environments.
For features that customers can access directly, we developed solutions that share hardware resources
across different software domains while maintaining security boundaries. This enables capabilities like
immediate rear camera display when shifting to reverse while ensuring these convenience features cannot
interfere with safety-critical functions. The software platform provides the abstraction layers and
development tools that allow our customers to focus on differentiating their vehicles rather than solving
low-level technical challenges.
These integrated technologies form a comprehensive platform enabling our customers to develop
advanced automotive systems efficiently and reliably. Our unified architecture, combined with
chip
capabilities and flexible software infrastructure, provides the foundation for the next generation of
intelligent and autonomous vehicles.

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
Our R&D Philosophy
Our R&D philosophy is rooted in customer-driven innovation and the latest technology development
trends. We emphasize on understanding real-world customer needs as well as the latest and emerging
technology, and maintaining close engagement throughout the development process. This enables us to
anticipate industry trends, validate product concepts, and ensure that our solutions deliver practical value
and sustained market competitiveness. We translate field constraints, including safety, latency, thermal
budgets, manufacturability and cost, into system requirements that guide both architecture and software
design.
A core feature of our approach is the combination of hardware and software innovation. We practice
system-level co-design, planning chip architecture, security subsystems, memory and I/O, and
accelerators, together with foundational software, virtualization and partitioning, toolchains and reference
applications. By co-designing chips and software, we ensure that new features and technologies are not
only advanced in theory but also effective in real-world deployments. This unified methodology aligns
silicon features with software roadmaps and safety/secure requirements, improves predictable
performance under representative workloads, reduces external components and bill of materials, and
accelerates bring-up and validation, thereby shortening time-to-market and lowering total implementation
cost.
Our R&D activities follow a staggered, multi-generation roadmap, balancing the enhancement of
existing products, active development of next-generation offerings, and exploration of cutting-edge
technologies. We provide reusable platforms and a unified software foundation, enabling smooth upgrades
across product generations while reducing rework and migration costs. While closely tracking emerging
trends such as generative and multi-modal AI, we remain committed to measurable improvements in
reliability, performance, and energy efficiency, validated against customer workloads and aligned with
functional safety and security processes
.
Our R&D Process
We identify potential R&D projects based on our development strategy and industry trends, as well
as the needs of our customers. Our R&D process is designed to ensure that every project is strategically
aligned and rigorously managed from concept to mass production. We begin with a structured project
selection stage, where each new initiative starts with a concise concept note outlining the requirements,
target specifications, feasibility, and required resources. Projects then undergo a thorough review to ensure
alignment with our overall strategy, and only those that meet our criteria move forward into formal
development. The following diagram illustrates our R&D process:

Outsourced R&D Arrangements
Our core R&D activities are conducted in-house by our experienced R&D team. In line with common
industry practice in the automotive semiconductor sector, we strategically outsource specific non-core
development tasks and labor-intensive activities, enabling our in-house R&D team to concentrate on core
technologies including SoC architecture design, heterogeneous multi-core computing optimization,
functional safety mechanisms, automotive-grade chip design and verification, and system-level
integration. To facilitate the R&D process, we utilize various items, tools and support services provided
from third-party suppliers, such as certain IP cores and EDA tools. IP cores procured from third-party
suppliers refer to ancillary functional blocks integrated into our SoCs, such as interface IPs and certain
processing units. We do not engage in the development of these ancillary IP cores procured from
third-party suppliers. Instead, we integrate these IPs into our SoC design and perform verification and
optimization to ensure they meet automotive-grade quality and performance standards. Such IP cores are
generally available from multiple qualified vendors. According to Frost & Sullivan, it is in line with the
industry norm for automotive semiconductor companies to procure ancillary IP cores from external
suppliers, allowing our in-house R&D team to focus on core differentiating technologies.
During the Track Record Period, we collaborated with qualified independent third-party service
providers for outsourced R&D arrangements. In 2020, during the early stage of our development, we
outsourced certain backend development of our SoCs to Supplier C. Such backend development services
primarily involved converting our completed designs into manufacturing-ready layouts for tape-out,
including design-for-testability and physical design activities. As our business expanded and our internal
R&D capacity strengthened, including through the recruitment of additional backend engineering
personnel, we progressively internalized these backend development activities. Such outsourcing
arrangements are common industry practice, particularly among early-stage fabless semiconductor
companies, as they allow companies to leverage specialized engineering resources and accelerate product
development prior to building in-house capabilities. Throughout this process, we have at all times retained
full ownership of all material intellectual property rights in relation to our SoCs, and such outsourcing
arrangements did not affect our ownership over the relevant IP .
In addition, we engage an outsourced service provider for PCB design and simulation for EVB. Such
technical service provider was selected based on their proven track record in automotive semiconductor

SALES AND MARKETING
Our Sales Network
Direct Sales
Through direct sales, we can understand customers’ technology and business development plan
firsthand, propose technical solutions and product selection, and help customers solve problems
efficiently. Our sales team is able to deliver value with an in-depth understanding of our customers’
businesses and industries.
Our sales efforts are centered on the needs of our customers. We leverage the collaborations among
our sales team, automotive OEMs and tier-one suppliers to identify customers’ needs. Our sales teams also
work closely with our product marketing team and R&D team to propose suitable products and solutions
to address the pain points faced by potential customers in the relevant industries.
As of
December 31, 2025, our sales team consisted of 15 employees with extensive industry
experience and in-depth expertise of our products and solutions. Our sales efforts covered major cities
across Chinese mainland, including Beijing, Shanghai, Changchun, Wuhan, Wuhu, Shenzhen and
Chongqing, allowing us to work closely with leading automotive customers in different regions. Through
these sales offices, our products have been adopted across a wide range of vehicle models both in China
and in various overseas market, such as Europe and Southeast Asia.
Sales Through Distributor
During the Track Record Period, we engaged
three distributors, including Customer H, for the sales
of our products and solutions, which was consistent with the industry practice. The revenue generated
through our engagement with the distributors accounted for less than 0.1% of our total revenue in 2024
and 2.3% of our total revenue in 2025.
Our relationships with the distributors were conducted on a seller-buyer basis, as they purchased our
products and solutions from us and then resold the products to customers. We recognized sales revenues
from the distributors when the control over our products and solutions was transferred to them.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we did not experience material
breach of the distribution agreement that had a significant impact on our business, nor did we have any
material disputes with or experience any return or exchange of products from
the distributors that had a
material adverse effect on our business.
To the best of our knowledge, during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date,
all of the distributors were Independent Third Parties. To the best of our knowledge, there is no other
relationship between the distributors and each of our Company, our subsidiaries, our Shareholders who
own 5% or more of our total issued Shares, Directors or senior management or any of their respective
associates, except for the business relationship between us and the distributors and Customer I, which was
also our supplier. See “— Overlapping of Our Customers and Suppliers” for details.
The following paragraphs set forth a summary of the salient terms of our arrangement with the
distributors:
 Term: The initial term of the distribution agreement is one year and will automatically renew
for successive one year term following the initial term. Both parties were allowed to terminate
the agreement for cause and we may terminate the agreement at will with 90-day prior written
notice.
 Pricing and payment terms : We determine our selling price to the distributors.
We require our
distributors to pay us 15 days prior to shipment, on delivery date, or within 30 days of shipment
unless otherwise agreed.

Pricing
We take into account various factors when determining the price of our products, including
production costs, technological differentiation, customer demand, supply chain dynamics, procurement
strategies and expected gross margins of each product. We also evaluate the competitive landscape,
including the overall market conditions as well as prices for similar products offered by our peers.
Furthermore, we determine the pricing of our service offerings on the number of personnel involved and
the complexity of the task at hand.
Branding
Our marketing department is responsible for enhancing our brand awareness and promoting both new
and existing products and solutions. We are committed to building a global brand associated with
technological innovation, and have adopted a comprehensive, multi-tiered marketing and branding
strategy. By leveraging a wide range of effective channels to reach potential customers, such as offline and
online events, and engaging with industry associations and standard-setting bodies, we strive to achieve
broad exposure and engagement across different audiences.
We focus on strengthening our brand image and corporate culture through targeted media
communication and by actively participating in various domestic and international exhibitions and
industry events. We also maintain close interactions with industry associations and standards-setting
bodies, and regularly host or attend technical seminars and forums each year. Within the automotive sector,
automotive OEMs play a pivotal role in the selection of chip suppliers for vehicle models. Therefore, we
actively engage in events hosted or attended by automotive OEMs to strengthen our brand influence and
technical engagement with them. This approach results in
stable partnership across the value chain.

ECARX Group adopted an annual fixed-fee arrangement for such services.
Our Collaboration with ECARX and Automotive OEMs
Our business collaboration with ECARX Group is based on a framework under which ECARX Group
procures our automotive-grade SoCs and integrates them into its domain controller platforms. These
platforms are then supplied by ECARX Group to automotive OEMs for installation in their vehicles. This
commercial flow results from the established structure of automotive supply chains rather than business
reliance on any particular tier-one supplier.
The automotive industry’s inherent complexity necessitates a structured division of responsibilities
among automotive OEMs, tier-one suppliers, and SoC providers. In the automotive manufacturing value
chain, tier-one suppliers and automotive SoC providers play fundamentally different but complementary
roles. Tier-one suppliers act as system integrators and direct suppliers to automotive OEMs, delivering
fully validated electronic control units (“ ECUs ”), domain controllers, or complete subsystems that meet
automotive functional safety, reliability, and vehicle-level integration requirements. By contrast,
automotive SoC providers — particularly those focused on intelligent cockpit and autonomous driving
chips — operate upstream as core computing platform providers, supplying high-performance,
automotive-grade SoCs that serve as the foundational hardware for vehicle intelligence. The following
table sets forth key differences between tier-one suppliers and SoC providers:

Under the current industry structure, SoC providers typically do not bypass tier-one suppliers to
directly supply chips to automotive OEMs. In addition to differing roles demonstrated above, the
integrated vehicle systems require hardware integration, software stacks, functional safety design, and
vehicle-level validation, which SoC providers typically do not deliver independently. Tier- one suppliers
are also responsible for system architecture design, hardware/software integration, functional safety,
cybersecurity, calibration, and long vehicle-level validation cycles, capabilities that most SoC vendors are
not structurally set up to equip. Furthermore, pricing, warranty, liability allocation, and change-
management mechanisms are deeply embedded in tier-one supply contracts, making direct SoC-to-OEM
delivery impractical under current procurement frameworks. However, automotive OEMs are increasingly
involved earlier at the chip-definition stage. Automotive OEMs now work more closely with SoC
providers on performance targets, computing architectures, and roadmaps to align chips with future
vehicle platforms.

Reasons for Our Customer Concentration on ECARX Group
Our high revenue concentration on ECARX Group during the Track Record Period can be primarily
attributed to following factors:
 Early-stage strategic collaboration with ECARX as a commercialization accelerator : Our
revenue concentration with ECARX Group during the Track Record Period should be assessed
in light of the industry structure of the automotive SoC segment and our early-stage
commercialization strategy. The intelligent cockpit domain controller market is characterized
by a relatively high degree of concentration, stringent technical requirements and
comparatively lower domestic SoC penetration. The development of automotive-grade SoCs
for this segment entails substantial upfront investment in advanced process nodes, licensed IP ,
and
system-level integration to meet software and functional requirements of automotive
OEMs. As a well-established tier-one supplier, ECARX Group maintains long-standing
collaborations with a broad base of domestic and international automotive OEMs,
and its
products are deployed across multiple vehicle platforms with wide market recognition. ECARX
Group sought to strengthen its supply chain resilience and product differentiation through the
development of domestic SoC capabilities, while we required a credible tier-one partner with
access to validated automotive OEM programs to accelerate product verification and market
entry. This alignment of strategic objectives formed the basis of our collaboration and made
ECARX Group a particularly suitable partner during our early commercialization stage.
Through this cooperation, our automotive-grade SoCs were validated against the rigorous
requirements of globally recognized automotive platforms, rather than being confined to
limited or experimental deployments, thereby generating meaningful market validation and
laying a solid foundation for broader customer adoption. As an early-stage automotive-grade
SoC provider, such close collaboration enabled us to shorten the time required for our products
to be deployed in vehicles.
This collaboration substantially reduced the lead time to
commercialization and allowed us to generate revenue at an earlier stage than would typically
be achievable for a start-up automotive SoC company
:
 By engaging with ECARX Group at the chip definition stage, we design our SoCs in
parallel with its domain controller architecture and vehicle system requirements, rather
than following a sequential development model. As both our chips and ECARX Group’s
domain controllers are designed in accordance with OEM specifications, this parallel
development approach shortens system-level validation and debugging cycles and
enables domain controllers incorporating our SoCs to more readily meet in-vehicle
requirements, thereby accelerating time to mass production.
 Under this collaboration model, during the engineering sample stage of our SoC
development, ECARX Group already initiates domain controller system design; and at
the customer sample stage of our SoC development, vehicle-level integration and testing
can begin, enabling the vehicle program to progress in parallel with chip validation. As
a result, in contrast to the conventional model where system design and vehicle testing
only commence after chip mass production, our chip validation process runs in parallel
with the vehicle programs, which, according to Frost & Sullivan, could shorten
commercialization by more than six months.

 Concentration at the tier-one level during scaling stages in alignment with industry practice :
From an industry perspective, revenue concentration at the tier-one level is not uncommon for
automotive SoC companies, particularly during early commercialization and scaling phases.
Tier-one suppliers typically act as solution integrators and channel semiconductor demand
across multiple vehicle models, and it is common for early-stage high-performance SoC
companies to generate a significant portion of revenue from a limited number of tier-one or
automotive OEM partners before customer diversification is achieved. Furthermore, the
automotive electronics and domain controller market is characterized by a relatively
concentrated tier-one supplier landscape. A limited number of tier-one suppliers account for a
substantial portion of system integration and domain controller programs across major
automotive OEM groups. As a result, SoC suppliers typically access automotive OEM vehicle
models primarily through these tier-one suppliers, which naturally leads to a degree of revenue
concentration at the tier-one level, particularly for companies at early commercialization or
scaling stages.

Basis for Business Sustainability
Our value proposition for ECARX
Despite the significant revenue concentration on ECARX Group, our relationship with ECARX
Group is underpinned by mutual achievements and a win-win cooperation, with low risk of termination,
for the following reasons:

Product strengths and deep early-stage collaboration : Our collaboration with ECARX Group
is underpinned by the inherent strength and long-term competitiveness of our automotive-grade
SoCs. See “— Our Competitive Strengths — Advanced, High-Performance and Reliable
Automotive-Grade SoCs” for details. These product capabilities position our automotive-grade
SoCs as a core, scalable and commercially viable solution for mass-market vehicle platforms,
where cost-performance efficiency, supply stability and development timelines are critical. By
providing a domestically developed alternative that balances computing performance, AI
acceleration capability and automotive-grade reliability with cost efficiency, our products
address fundamental tier-one and automotive OEM needs across multiple vehicle programs.
This enduring product value proposition has supported and will continue to support adoption
by ECARX Group across successive vehicle models and underpins the sustainability of our
business relationship notwithstanding the historical revenue concentration.
In addition, from an early stage of our chip design process, we engaged in close and continuous
technical collaboration with ECARX Group. Through this early-stage interaction, we were able
to obtain timely feedback on system-level requirements, software architecture considerations
and vehicle program planning, and reflect such inputs into our SoC design and feature
definition where appropriate. In addition, we supported customization at the chip and system
integration level through which ECARX Group was able to more efficiently and effectively
implement the functionalities required for its domain controller solutions and vehicle
programs.
 High switching costs : The selection of a core automotive-grade SoC is a prolonged and
resource-intensive process that involves extensive hardware-software co-development, multi-
stage validation and system-level optimization across operating systems, middleware,
peripheral components and vehicle-level integration. Such processes typically span multiple
development phases and are closely aligned with an automotive OEM’s vehicle platform
development and launch timelines. Once a core SoC platform has been selected and validated
for a given vehicle platform, significant time and cost are incurred to complete vehicle-level
testing, performance tuning, thermal and power optimization, as well as automotive-grade
functional safety and reliability certification. Replacing an automotive SoC typically entails
redesigning domain controller hardware, re-integrating operating systems and middleware,
migrating and adapting large-scale automotive software stacks, and re-optimizing system
performance. Specifically, vehicle software systems are large in scale and deeply integrated
with hardware, and migrating to a new SoC platform requires extensive functional porting,
application adaptation, compatibility testing, and performance tuning. The new SoC platforms
must also undergo lengthy functional safety (e.g., ISO 26262), reliability, and vehicle-level
validation processes before approval for mass production. Replacing an SoC would therefore
take approximately 12 months, according to Frost & Sullivan, which may materially delay
vehicle launches, disrupt platform development schedules and increase overall project costs. In
addition,
the development costs for a new SoC platform typically reach tens of millions of
Renminbi, according to Frost & Sullivan. As a result, both automotive OEMs and tier-one
suppliers generally adopt a prudent and cautious approach when considering changes to a
validated SoC platform, and are unlikely to pursue such replacement absent a fundamental
change in vehicle requirements or platform strategy.
 Strategic relevance of our products to ECARX Group’s historical and future automotive
OEM expansion : In the automotive industry, chipset selection and functional definition are
increasingly led by automotive OEMs at the vehicle-platform level, while tier-one suppliers are
responsible for integrating the selected chipsets into domain controllers and other system-level
