When selecting suppliers, we employ a multi-dimensional evaluation system that assesses both
technical capabilities and business qualifications. We evaluate suppliers’ technological expertise, R&D
strength, and ability to support our product roadmap, including their experience in automotive-grade
products, process technology maturity, and capacity for collaborative innovation. Quality management is
paramount, and we require suppliers to demonstrate
reliable quality management systems, preferably with
certifications such as ISO 9001, IA TF 16949 for automotive suppliers, and other relevant industry
standards. We thoroughly assess their quality control processes, defect rates, and continuous improvement
practices. Beyond technical capabilities, we verify suppliers’ business credentials including business
licenses, financial stability, legal compliance, and adherence to environmental, social, and governance
standards. Suppliers must meet applicable regulatory requirements and demonstrate ethical business
practices. We also evaluate production capacity, scalability, and track record in meeting delivery
commitments, as reliability in supply continuity is critical given the automotive industry’s stringent
requirements. While cost competitiveness is considered in the context of total cost of ownership, we
prioritize quality, reliability, and service levels. Market reputation, customer references, and industry
recognition serve as additional indicators of supplier reliability and service quality.
Our supplier qualification process follows a structured approach beginning with initial assessment
based on documentation review and capability evaluation, followed by on-site audits for critical suppliers
to verify manufacturing facilities, quality systems, and operational processes. Prospective suppliers
provide samples for testing and validation to ensure products meet our technical specifications and quality
standards. Selected suppliers may be engaged for trial production runs to assess performance under actual
operating conditions before formal qualification. Suppliers meeting all criteria are formally approved and
added to our qualified supplier list.
Procurement and Supplier Management
For mass production requirements, we generally enter into framework agreements with qualified
vendors that establish general terms and conditions including commercial terms, quality requirements,
delivery schedules, pricing mechanisms, and payment terms. These framework agreements provide the
overarching structure while allowing flexibility through specific purchase orders that detail quantities,
delivery dates, and other transaction-specific requirements. We also typically include confidentiality and
intellectual property protection provisions in our supplier agreements, or enter into separate non-
disclosure agreements with our suppliers, which set out the respective rights and obligations relating to
the ownership and protection of our intellectual properties, technical knowhow and trade secrets. These
agreements typically span multiple years, fostering stable partnerships that enable joint planning,
continuous improvement, and mutual growth. For software components and services, we typically contract
on a project basis with terms tailored to the specific scope, deliverables, intellectual property
arrangements, and performance milestones.
We maintain active supplier relationships through continuous performance monitoring and
collaborative improvement. We regularly assess supplier performance across key metrics including
quality, delivery, responsiveness, and cost through periodic reviews that help identify areas for
improvement. Our quality assurance program includes incoming quality inspections, defect rate
monitoring, and collaborative implementation of corrective and preventive actions when issues arise.
Regular business reviews, technical exchanges, and joint problem-solving sessions strengthen partnerships
and drive continuous improvement. We actively monitor supply chain risks including single-source
dependencies, geopolitical factors, and financial stability of key suppliers, employing contingency
planning and dual-sourcing strategies to mitigate potential disruptions. For strategic suppliers, we may
provide technical support, co-development opportunities, and capacity building assistance to enhance their
capabilities and alignment with our technology roadmap. We prioritize supply chain resilience through
diversification, strategic inventory management, and proactive risk mitigation, balancing efficiency with
security of supply, which is particularly critical for automotive applications where reliability and
continuity are paramount.

Supply Chain Management and Risk Mitigation
The global foundry market is characterized by high technological barriers to entry and significant
concentration among a few leading providers, particularly for cutting-edge process nodes. While qualified
manufacturers with comparable technical capabilities and production processes exist both domestically
and abroad across our manufacturing requirements, the concentrated nature of the foundry market and
technical complexity of our products may expose us to certain supply chain risks. Additionally, the
qualification and onboarding of new manufacturing contractors requires substantial time and resources due
to the technical complexity of our products and solutions. We actively manage key manufacturing risks
including potential capacity constraints, geopolitical factors affecting technology transfer, and evolving
regulatory requirements for advanced processes. We have established a diverse foundry supplier network,
initially beginning our cooperation with Supplier F before strategically expanding to include several other
foundry partners, guided by our supplier pool policies which emphasize technological capabilities,
production capacity, and reliability.
Notwithstanding the establishment of our diverse supplier network, a significant portion of our
procurement remains concentrated with Supplier B, primarily due to Supplier B’s technological leadership
in the advanced process nodes required for our products. Compared to other market players, Supplier B
offers superior yield rates, production maturity, and capacity scale in these specific nodes. While our
broader supplier network provides operational resilience, particularly for mature nodes and non-core
components, other foundry partners cannot be readily deployed to replace Supplier B for our core
advanced node products on similar or better terms in the near term. This is primarily due to the substantial
switching costs involved, including the need for extensive product redesign and re-qualification, as well
as the potential commercial risks associated with lower yield rates or capacity instability at alternative
foundries. For mature node components and specific application scenarios, we are actively diversifying
our supply chain by engaging with a broader range of regional and local suppliers to secure more favorable
cost structures and delivery terms. As the manufacturing capabilities of other international foundries and
local suppliers mature, we expect the feasibility of broader diversification to increase significantly, with
the ultimate objective of establishing a resilient supply ecosystem anchored by Supplier B for advanced
technologies while being supported by a diverse network of auxiliary suppliers for other needs.

IP Cores and EDA Tools
IP cores and EDA tools are essential to our integrated circuit design and commercialization
processes. IP cores are modular chip components that allow us to incorporate proven hardware designs into
our products without developing every component from scratch. EDA tools support the full design
workflow, from design input and verification to preparation for mass production, and help translate design
logic into physical silicon implementation. They also enable the automated design, simulation and
validation of complex circuits that would be impractical to perform manually. These technologies are
critical to our operations because they improve efficiency, shorten development cycles and support faster
commercialization. By using third-party IP cores, we can focus more of our research and development
resources on proprietary innovation. EDA tools also help us ensure design feasibility, control costs and
identify potential defects before manufacturing. Given their importance to industry compatibility and
manufacturing requirements, we actively manage the procurement of these key tools.
We select IP cores and EDA tool suppliers based on their industry-specific expertise, reputation and
their technical capabilities and reliability. We typically enter into licensing agreements with these
suppliers, and the salient terms of our licensing agreements with them are set out below:
 Licensing arrangement : We are generally granted with non-transferable, non-assignable and
non-exclusive license for using the IP cores and EDA tools.
 Payment terms : We are generally required to pay the licensing fees for IP cores and EDA
software within 30 or 45 days from the respective license start date. The term of each license
is typically one year.
 Support Services : Suppliers generally provide support services during the respective IP core
licensing period.
 Delivery. IP cores and EDA tools are generally delivered electronically alongside their
corresponding documentation and license keys on the respective license start date.
 Termination : Either party may terminate the agreement for cause upon providing prior written
notice.
Pricing for our IP and EDA procurements is negotiated based on factors such as technology
complexity, process nodes and market rates. Payment terms typically include upfront licensing fees,
annual maintenance fees and per-chip royalties, payable in accordance with contractually agreed
schedules. Per-chip royalties are payable on an ongoing basis in connection with product sales throughout
the chip’s life cycle. Upfront licensing fees and annual maintenance fees incurred during the research and
development phase are recorded as intangible assets or research and development expenses, while per-chip
royalties are recorded as cost of revenue. We generally seek to recover these costs through our product
pricing and, where applicable, royalties charged to downstream customers.

COMPETITION
The automotive-grade SoC market is characterized by rapid technological evolution, stringent
automotive quality and safety requirements, and high barriers to entry. International companies still
dominate the market by virtue of their first mover advantage, while domestic companies are accelerating
their catch-up efforts. We mainly compete with specific intelligent cockpit and autonomous driving SoC
providers, general chip providers and automotive OEM self-developers. We face increasingly intense
competition with other leading players in various aspects of our business, including product design,
computing power and intelligent functions. For details, see “Risk Factors — Risks Relating to the
Commercialization of Our Products and Solutions — The industry in which we operate is highly
competitive and rapidly evolving.
We believe that the automotive-grade SoC market presents substantial
barriers to entry for potential competitors, which include advanced technology capabilities, significant
capital requirements, established customer relationships, specialized talent, and comprehensive ecosystem
partnerships. For more information
, see “Industry Overview.”

may be subject to a fine between RMB1,000 and RMB10,000 per lease for any delay in making these
registrations.
Therefore, we have the right to use such properties in accordance with the lease agreement
but we may be subject to the risks of fines if the lease registration is not completed as required by the
relevant local housing administrative authorities. The maximum aggregate amount of potential
administrative penalties we would be subject to for these two lease agreements is RMB20,000. As of the
Latest Practicable Date, we were not subject to any penalties arising from the non-registration of the lease
agreements. In the unlikely event that we are forced to relocate from these properties, given that there are
sufficient comparable premises available in the market, we do not anticipate any material difficulty in
finding alternative locations. We expect the time and costs required for such relocation to be immaterial.
As of December 31, 2025, none of the properties leased by us had a carrying amount of 15% or more

INTERNATIONAL SANCTIONS AND THE U.S. OUTBOUND INVESTMENT SECURITY
PROGRAM
U.S. Export Control and International Sanctions
We procured certain items subject to the EAR that are either controlled solely for anti-terrorism
reasons or classified as EAR99 (“ Procured Items ”). During the Track Record Period, we procured IP
cores and EDA tools from the United States, and the procurement amount was RMB105.9 million,
RMB79.4 million and RMB58.0 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.
As advised by our legal advisors as to the U.S. Outbound Investment Rule and export control, given
that during the Track Record Period, (i) we did not purchase any items subject to the EAR which require
a license for us to procure; (ii) we did not supply any of the Procured Items to any of the Crimea region,
Cuba, Iran, Luhansk People’s Republic and Donetsk People’s Republic regions, North Korea and Syria,
as well as Russia and Belarus (collectively, the “ AT Sanctioned Countries ”); (iii) we have not engaged
in transactions that involve or benefit any “military end-users” or “military end-use”; (iv) our activities
did not involve certain prohibited end-uses set forth in section 744.23 of the EAR, our procurements of
such Procured Items during the Track Record Period did not represent a violation of the applicable U.S.
export controls. Based on the above and considering that our production, development timelines, customer
orders and commercialization have not been affected in relation to the Procured Items, the Directors are
of the view that our business operations and financial performance have not been materially and adversely
affected due to the Procured Items. See “— Suppliers — IP Cores and EDA Tools” for alternative and
substitute arrangements for our IP cores and EDA tools.
Since January 16, 2025, our products are subject to a presumption that they are classified as 3A090.a
(“3A090 Presumption ”). As advised by our legal advisors as to the U.S. Outbound Investment Rule and
export control, on the basis that our products are packaged by an approved OSA T company who confirms
that the approximate transistor count of the final packaged integrated circuit is below 30 billion transistors,
the 3A090 Presumption is overcome. Further, given that our products are not of controlled U.S.-origin and
did not contain more than the de minimis value of U.S.-origin content (including the Procured Items), as
advised by our legal advisors as to the U.S. Outbound Investment Rule and export control, our products
are not subject to the EAR. Based on the above and considering that we have not experienced any tariff
fluctuations, order cancellations or order re-negotiation in relation to the EAR, the Directors are of the
opinion that the EAR has not had any material adverse effect on our operations and financial performance.
Based on the due diligence conducted, nothing has come to the attention of the Joint Sponsors that would
cause them to reasonably cast doubt on the aforesaid view expressed by the Directors.

The U.S. Outbound Investment Security Program
On October 28, 2024, the Department of the Treasury issued the Provisions Pertaining to U.S.
Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of Concern (the “ Final
Rule ”), which became effective on January 2, 2025. The Final Rule implements a regulatory framework
for certain U.S. investments into China (including Hong Kong and Macau) in entities engaged in activities
involving (i) semiconductors and microelectronics, (ii) quantum information technologies, and (iii)
artificial intelligence systems with applications that pose national security risks, collectively defined as
“Covered Foreign Persons.” The program would prohibit U.S. persons from undertaking certain
transactions and require notification by U.S. persons on certain investments in Covered Foreign Persons.
We are engaged in the design of integrated circuits. As advised by our legal advisors as to the U.S.
Outbound Investment Rule and export control, given that certain of our integrated circuits (which are not
for data centre use) meet or exceed the performance parameters in ECCN 3A090.a.2, we are likely to be
deemed as a Covered Foreign Person engaged in “Covered Activities” referred to in the definition of
“Prohibited Transaction” as set out in 31 C.F.R. § 850.224(c). Nonetheless, it is expected that U.S. persons
will be able to purchase our H Shares publicly traded on the Stock Exchange following the Global Offering
without being subject to any notification required or be outright prohibited based on the publicly traded
securities exception under the Final Rule, as long as the investments made do not afford the U.S. persons
rights that go beyond standard minority shareholder protections. Nonetheless, as acquisition of our equity
interests by U.S. persons may constitute a prohibited transaction (unless an exception such as the publicly
traded securities exception mentioned above applies), the Final Rule may increase the compliance burden
of U.S. investors and may cause U.S. investors to adopt a more cautious approach in their investments,
which may negatively impact our ability to raise capital from U.S. investors.
Tariffs
Our current product portfolio comprises primarily our intelligent cockpit SoC and solution, which
accounted for 99.8%, 100.0% and 97.1% of our total revenue in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. Our
intelligent cockpit SoCs and solutions are sold directly to customers located in the PRC and, to a much
lesser extent, we also provided development services for customers located in Singapore , and such
development services are not subject to tariff regimes in both China and Singapore. The tier-one suppliers
integrate such SoCs into domain controllers and other automotive electronic control units before supplying
the finished products to automotive OEMs. To the best of our knowledge, our tier-one customers do not
deliver their products incorporating our SoCs to automotive OEMs in the United States, and the
automotive OEMs do not sell vehicles incorporating our SoCs into the United States. In addition, due to
regulatory, policy and market access constraints, vehicles manufactured by PRC-based OEMs are
generally not exported to the United States. Accordingly, we believe that the end products incorporating
our SoCs are not destined for the U.S. market, and therefore U.S. tariffs are not applicable to our products,
nor are any such U.S.- related tariff costs borne by us.
To the extent that vehicles incorporating our SoCs are exported outside the PRC, any applicable
import tariffs would, as a matter of industry practice, be assessed at the vehicle or end-product level. Such

RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL
The objectives of our risk management system are to: (i) identify potential events that may impact
us, ensuring relevant risks are controlled within acceptable and appropriate levels relative to our
objectives; (ii) facilitate accurate and reliable communication of information to both internal and external
stakeholders of our Company; (iii) ensure compliance with our business operations; (iv) enhance the
efficiency and effectiveness of our business activities, thereby reducing uncertainties in achieving
operational goals; and (v) establish crisis management plans for significant risks to protect our Company
from substantial losses due to catastrophic risks or human errors.
Our Audit Committee is responsible for reviewing the regulations and primary objectives related to
risk management, submitting an annual comprehensive risk management report to the Board, reviewing
risk management strategies and solutions for significant risks, and addressing other matters related to
comprehensive risk management as authorized by the Board. Our internal audit department is tasked with
implementing our risk management policies and systems. Other departments and business units are
supervised by the internal audit department in their risk management efforts.
The typical operating procedures of our risk management work include the following: (i) collecting
information related to risk management, including historical data and future forecasts. Specifically, in
terms of strategic risk, we extensively gather cases where domestic and international companies have
suffered losses due to uncontrolled strategic risks; in financial risk, we collect cases of financial crises
caused by uncontrolled financial risks; in market risk, we gather cases where companies have suffered
losses due to neglecting market risks and lacking response measures; in operational risk, we collect
information relevant to our Company and industry; and in legal risk, we gather cases where companies
have suffered losses due to neglecting legal and regulatory risks and lacking response measures; (ii)
assessing the significance and likelihood (or frequency and probability) of risks; (iii) senior management
assists the Board in determining a unified risk appetite and tolerance based on business characteristics, and
establishes risk warning lines and corresponding countermeasures; (iv) senior management formulates risk
management solutions for significant risks based on risk management strategies; and (v) senior
management supervises the implementation of risk management, making timely improvements based on
changes and any deficiencies. Our approach also involves the continuous enhancement of internal control
mechanisms and regular reviews of our risk management policies and internal control measures to
maintain their effectiveness and adequacy, ensuring that our operations align with industry standards and
regulatory requirements.

Data Collection and Destruction
We collect personal information regarding employees, candidates, and contact persons of our
cooperating parties only when a lawful basis exists, and we do not collect any data from our customers.
Upon the fulfillment of the intended processing purposes or the expiration of the agreed storage period,
we promptly delete the relevant data.
Data Processing
Access to the original data through the database is only permitted with due procedures, and the
relevant personnel must keep confidentiality of the data they access. When business personnel need to
access data, they are required to submit a written application for approval by the relevant department head
and the IT department head, after which the request will be handled by the IT department for unified query
and data extraction. After accessing the data, business personnel are required to ensure that such data is
used properly within the scope of the approved access, and must not misuse the data or breach
confidentiality obligations. Business personnel shall not add, modify or delete original data in the database
without permission. When the data needs to be modified due to business needs or bug fixing, a written
application shall be submitted for unified arrangement of corresponding modification after the approval
of the department head. When modifying the data, the feasibility and safety should be fully demonstrated
and the modification plan should be determined before the modification is carried out to ensure that the
system is error-free after the data is modified.
Data Storage, Encryption and Backup
Access to the database and backup files should be strictly controlled, and unauthorized access to the
data and backup files is strictly prohibited. The backup data must be safely stored and the storage media
cannot be placed on the desktop or other exposed places. We use a variety of technologies to protect the
data we collect, including encryption and data backup measures. We determine the data protection level
based on our risk assessment, and assign corresponding measures to each level taking into consideration
the type and property of encryption algorithms and the length of the password used. We routinely review
and amend our encryption policies as appropriate, and ensure important information must be encrypted
when transmitted. We maintain data backups for core application systems in two or more copies. Daily
backup shall be performed for business-related data. We conduct mandatory system and data backup
before and after substantial upgrade of the systems.

Environmental Management
As we do not operate any production facilities, we aim to control energy consumption and reduce
carbon emissions in our offices. As outlined in our ESG Comprehensive Management System, we
encourage our employees to turn off computer monitors, lights and non-essential office equipment when
leaving for extended periods. We also encourage employees to utilize natural lighting to reduce power
consumption of lighting equipment. When upgrading lighting equipment, we prioritize energy-saving LED
lighting to improve energy efficiency.
To optimize water resource utilization, water supply facilities are

BUSINESS SUSTAINABILITY AND PATH TO PROFITABILITY
We had achieved business growth but were loss-making during the Track Record Period. Our revenue
increased from RMB110.8 million in 2023 to RMB234.5 million in 2024 and further to RMB341.8 million,
representing a CAGR of 75.6% . However, we recorded loss for the year of RMB838.5 million, RMB910.1

Reasons for Historical Loss
The development and commercialization of automotive-grade SoCs are characterized by significant
upfront investments and long product commercialization cycles, which posed challenges to achieving
profitability during our early years of operation. We incurred net losses during the Track Record Period,
primarily attributable to the following reasons:
 Significant upfront investment in R&D initiatives : Our R&D spending primarily focused on
developing new product and variants, as well as enhancing existing products to support broader
vehicle models and application scenarios. While these efforts are essential to strengthening our
long-term market competitiveness, our products are still in the early stages of
commercialization and revenue generation, and the long development and customer
certification cycles associated with automotive-grade SoCs mean that our R&D spending has
not yet translated into significant revenue growth, contributing to our net losses during the
Track Record Period. During the Track Record Period, we made significant investments to
build our core technology stack
and incurred research and development expenses of RMB594.5
million, RMB583.2 million and RMB 584.1 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively,
accounting for 536.6%, 248.7% and 170.9% of our total revenue in the same periods,
respectively.
 Limited economies of scale : We have achieved substantial growth during the Track Record
Period and generated economies of scale through streamlined R&D process, technology reuse
enabled by unified chip architecture and organization structure optimization. Our operating
expenses, defined as the sum of research and development expenses, administrative expenses
and selling and marketing expenses, as a percentage of total revenue decreased from
651.5%
in 2023 to 301.1% in 2024 and to 217.9% in 2025. Despite the decrease in our operating
expenses as a percentage of total revenue, we expect economies of scale to remain limited in
the near term due to substantial upfront investments required in such a fast-moving and highly
competitive industry.

OVERVIEW
As of the Latest Practicable Date, Mobile & Magic Limited (“ M&M”) held approximately 18.55%
of our total issued share capital, being our single largest Shareholder. M&M is wholly owned by Future
Magic Capital Limited, which is wholly owned by ECARX Holdings Inc. (1), a company listed on the
NASDAQ (ticker symbol: ECX) (“ ECARX Holdings ”). Therefore, M&M, Future Magic Capital Limited,
and ECARX Holdings collectively control approximately 18.55% of the voting rights in our Company.
Immediately following the completion the Global Offering (assuming the Over-Allotment Option is not
exercised), M&M, Future Magic Capital Limited, and ECARX Holdings collectively control
approximately [
15.76]% of the voting rights in our Company and will remain as the single largest group
of Shareholders of our Company (the “ Single Largest Group of Shareholders ”).
ECARX GROUP AS OUR LARGEST CUSTOMER AND A KEY STRATEGIC PARTNER
ECARX Group is a leading tier-one supplier specializing in intelligent vehicle computing platforms
and domain controllers. According to Frost & Sullivan, ECARX Group’s products have been widely
adopted by multiple prominent automotive OEMs in China and internationally, and ECARX Group is a
leading tier-one system integrator, providing domain controller platforms and related solutions to
automotive OEMs. During the Track Record Period, ECARX Group was our largest customer and a key
strategic partner, contributing a substantial portion of our total revenues. Revenues generated from
ECARX Group amounted to
RMB109.9 million, RMB230.4 million and RMB 329.0 million in 2023, 2024
and 2025, respectively, representing 99.2%, 98.2% and 96.3% of our total revenue for the same periods,
respectively. Our business collaboration with ECARX Group is based on a framework under which
ECARX Group procures our automotive SoC products and integrates them into its domain controller
platforms. These platforms are then supplied by ECARX Group to automotive OEMs for installation in
their vehicle models.
Our high revenue concentration on ECARX Group during the Track Record Period
can be primarily attributed to the following factors: (a) early-stage strategic collaboration with ECARX
Group as a commercialization accelerator; (b) market alignment driving demand concentration during the
production ramp-up phase; and (c) concentration at the tier-one level during scaling stages in alignment
with industry practice.
Despite the significant revenue concentration on ECARX Group, our relationship
with ECARX Group is underpinned by mutual achievements and a win-win cooperation, with low risk of
termination, for the following reasons: (a) robust product value and deep early-stage collaboration; (b)
high switching costs; and (c) strategic relevance of our products to ECARX Group’s historical and future
automotive OEM expansion.
In addition to our collaboration with ECARX Group, our business sustainability is further supported
by expanding engagements with a broader range of automotive OEMs and tier-one suppliers. Consistent
with prevailing industry practices, we continue to prioritize direct engagement with automotive OEMs to
align our product development and platform roadmap with OEM-level vehicle strategies, while
progressively diversifying collaborations with tier-one suppliers for system integration and program
execution:(a) broadening automotive OEM engagement base; (b) diversification of tier-one supplier
collaboration; (c) increasing contribution from non-ECARX-Group tie-one suppliers; and (d) product
roadmap supporting further tier-one diversification.
For a detailed disclosure of our business relationship
with ECARX Group, please also see “Business — Customers — Our Relationship with ECARX Group”.

resolutions and shall not be counted in the quorum for the voting;

Reasons for the Transactions
ECARX Group is one of our major customers and a strategic partner committed to long-term
collaboration. Leveraging ECARX Group’s strong market presence and growing global presence in the
smart vehicle sector, the transactions contemplated under the framework agreement enables our Group to
scale the adoption of our automotive-grade SoCs and related software solutions, thereby enhancing market
penetration and brand recognition.
Over the years, we have developed integrated product development workflows with ECARX Group,
enabling faster SoC integration, shorter R&D iteration cycles, and improved system stability and
performance. This alignment enhances ECARX Group’s ability to meet time-to-market pressures while
also providing our Group with valuable feedback for ongoing platform optimization and product
innovation. ECARX Group has developed its intelligent cockpit and cockpit-parking integrated solutions
based on our SE1000 series products and secured program nomination from automotive OEM customers,
and has been supplying to such customers on an ongoing basis.
Additionally, the continuous transactions support mutual operational efficiency. Our Group and
ECARX Group have established standardized operational protocols, which streamline logistics, reduce
communication frictions, and help mitigate supply chain risks, particularly in the context of increasingly
complex and time-sensitive vehicle production cycles.
For details, please see “Business — Our Relationship with ECARX Group.”
Pricing Policies
The consideration payable by ECARX Group for procurement of SoCs from our Group is determined
based on normal commercial terms and on an arm’s length basis, and is consistent with the pricing
mechanisms adopted in similar transactions with Independent Third Parties.
For sales of SoCs, we determine pricing based on market comparable products, especially the
competing ones. In addition, we factor in our internal cost of production, including direct material costs,
packaging, testing and validation, engineering support, royalty fees for software usage embedded in the
SoCs and allocated manufacturing overheads.
In determining the specific pricing for ECARX Group, our Group also takes into account historical
pricing offered to ECARX Group for similar or equivalent products, adjusted for inflation, changes in
component cost structures, and any enhancements in product functionality or performance. Additionally,
we conduct benchmarking analysis with pricing charged to Independent Third Party customers under
similar commercial terms, such as
purchase volumes, delivery schedules, product specifications, and
after-sale support commitments. This multi-factor approach ensures that pricing remains market-aligned,
non-preferential, and commercially reasonable.

2. Providing Technical Support Services to ECARX Group
Principal Terms
Pursuant to the Product and Service Procurement Framework Agreement, our Group agreed to
provide technical support services to assist ECARX Group for post-authorization product development
after our supply of general products and software, including on-site and remote support by our technical
engineer teams, case follow-up and resolution via the designated feedback support system interface and
laboratory training to assist ECARX Group in completing solution integration and product development
based on our SoC modules. In consideration, ECARX Group shall pay our Group technical support fees
accordingly.
Reasons for the Transactions
The provision of technical support services to ECARX Group is an essential and recurring part of
our Group’s business model as a leading automotive-grade SoC solutions provider. Given the technical
complexity, extensive interfaces and large-scale architecture of our SoC products, customers typically
require our assistance during their subsequent development to address queries and issues arising from the
use of technical parameters, function/procedure calls, SDKs, drivers and related integration matters.
The aforementioned services are necessary to support ECARX Group in completing post-
authorization product development, including software-hardware integration, system optimization, and
performance validation, after the supply of our SoC modules. This transaction is in line with common
industry practice, where tier-one customers expect continuous technical engagement from their SoC
suppliers throughout the product lifecycle. After the customer’s intelligent cockpit or driving solutions are
launched into vehicles, we usually expect to receive continuing customer feedback and are required to
provide ongoing after-sales technical support and related services. By providing such support, we enhance
customer satisfaction, encourage long-term cooperation, and strengthen the reputation and adoption of our
SoC platforms across the ecosystem.
During the Track Record Period, we offered on-site, remote assistance and targeted training to
authorized customers integrating our SoCs, including ECARX Group, thereby ensuring consistency in
quality and enhances our product reputation and ecosystem adoption.
For details, please see “Business — Our Relationship with ECARX Group.”
Pricing Policies
The consideration payable by ECARX Group for technical support services of our Group is
determined through arm’s length negotiations. In determining the pricing, we take into account a number
of commercially relevant factors, including:
(i) the scope and complexity of the detailed technical support requirements;
(ii) the estimated time and level of engagement required from our technical engineering teams,
including number of on-site visits, remote troubleshooting sessions and lab-based testing
support, taking into account personnel costs and target gross margin level;

driven by additional technical support needs arising from expanded and diversified future
product portfolio;
(ii) ECARX Group continues to deploy our SoCs across its expanding product portfolio in different
countries and regions, leading to higher post-deployment support demand, including software
patching, version upgrades, system tuning and customer-specific integration services
.I n
specific, our Company introduces annual iterations and upgrades to SDKs and localized
deployment of large language models. These advanced functionalities, delivered through
software iterations, are expected to drive sustained demand and increased transaction amounts
for technical support services in the coming years;
(iii) based on the ongoing commercial discussions and ECARX Group’s product roadmap, we

expected to generate significant technical support demand, such as training, Q&A and on-site
assistance ; and
(iv) the automotive electronics industry is experiencing a shift towards software-defined vehicles
(SDVs), requiring over-the-air (OTA) support and continuous integration. SoC platforms used
in modern vehicles now often serve multiple domains (e.g., infotainment, ADAS, connectivity),
necessitating multi-dimensional support beyond initial deployment. This transformation,
driven by the transition from hardware-centered functionality to software iteration as the core,
is expected to create ongoing multi-dimensional technical support demand.
3. Providing Licensing and Development Services to ECARX Group
Principal Terms
Pursuant to the Product and Service Procurement Framework Agreement, our Group agreed to grant
software and technology license to ECARX Group and provide customized development services based on
ECARX Group’s requirements. In consideration, ECARX Group shall pay our Group licensing fees and
software customization fees accordingly.
Reasons for the Transactions
The software and technology developed by our Group contain proprietary intellectual property, and
the use of such software by ECARX Group in its commercial products requires a formal software license.
These licenses allow ECARX Group to legally access, deploy, and maintain the software within their
SoC-integrated hardware platforms in accordance with agreed usage rights and technical parameters.

In the context of intelligent cockpit and domain controller development, ECARX Group requires a
high level of software-hardware integration to ensure optimal system performance, reliability, and
compliance with evolving functional safety and cybersecurity standards. Our SoCs are designed with a
high degree of architectural flexibility and are equipped with a suite of self-developed foundational
software components, including but not limited to bootloaders, BSPs, middleware layers, real-time
operating systems (RTOS), and security frameworks. These components are integral to enabling the core
functions of the SoC platform, including power management, display rendering, sensor fusion, and secure
communication.
Given the technical complexity and application-specific nature of ECARX Group’s product roadmap,
there is a need for customized development services to adapt and optimize our software platform to
ECARX Group’s specific use cases. This includes tailoring the software to the design requirements of
ECARX Group’s intelligent cockpit domain controllers, in-vehicle infotainment systems, and connectivity
modules. Through such adaptation, ECARX Group can reduce time-to-market, enhance system stability,
and support feature differentiation in a competitive automotive marketplace.
The transaction also reflects industry-standard practices in the automotive semiconductor ecosystem,
where SoC providers license accompanying software and offer customization services to tier-one
customers and automotive-OEM-aligned solution integrators. The ongoing collaboration between our
Group and ECARX Group in this regard enhances our ecosystem influence, promotes deeper product
integration, and supports long-term customer engagement, and ensures that our personnel costs and
resource allocations for the project are reasonable.
For details, please see “Business — Our Relationship
with ECARX Group.”
Pricing Policies
The consideration payable by ECARX Group for software and technology licensing is determined
based on normal commercial terms and on an arm’s length basis, taking into account the prevailing market
conditions by reference to the rates offered to Independent Third Parties for similar transactions.
For software customized development services, the pricing is primarily determined the man-hours
and expertise committed by our engineering team, technical complexity and novelty of the customization
work, scope of deliverables (including documentation, testing and integration support), and our Group’s
long-term commercialization strategy for the customized components, including whether the deliverables
may be reused or productized for other customers in the future.

increase in licensing and development projects, a substantial growth trajectory of transaction

offerings in different countries and regions.
Key areas include (i) foundational platform
development, including GKI (General Kernel Image) support, Linux Kernel upgrades, Android
version upgrades and virtualization of other operating systems; (ii) ecosystem and hardware
adaptation, including GAS (Google Automotive Services) integration, Audio DSP AWE (Audio
Weaver Engine) dual-core support, ISP solution development and IQ (Image Quality) Tuning
tools and A VL (Approved V endor List) validation for new hardware components; (iii) reference
designs and key subsystem work across product tiers, including entry-level cockpit platforms,
enhanced cockpit platforms, and integrated cockpit and driving convergence solutions. The
scope and deliverables of these projects are expected to significantly drive future transaction
volumes ;
(iii) ECARX Group’s product roadmap and platform iteration plan, including anticipated model
launches and platform upgrades based on our SoCs, typically require incremental
customization and comprehensive adaption. Each new platform iteration, especially those
involving different compute nodes, display architectures, or OS environments, typically
requires tuning of our Group’s base software packages. These recurring engineering
requirements are expected to generate sustained demand for both licensing and development
services as ECARX Group expands its product offerings and procurement of SoCs from our
Group; and
(iv) the broader automotive industry is undergoing a transformation towards software-defined
vehicle architectures, where cockpit and driving functions increasingly rely on deeply
integrated SoC platforms. This trend has led to greater reliance on upstream software stack
providers, particularly for foundational system software. As SoCs become more advanced and
feature-rich, the need for licensing of software IP and customized adaption becomes more
pronounced. Key drivers include virtualization for multi-domain operations, dual-SoC
interconnect for cross-domain integration, and middleware for platform stability. These
industry dynamics support a structurally increasing demand profile for our Group’s licenses
and development services.

LISTING RULES IMPLICATIONS
One-off Connected Transaction
As the Technology Licensing Agreement was entered into prior to the Listing and the transactions
thereunder are one-off in nature, the reporting, announcement, annual review and independent
Shareholders’ approval requirements with respect to continuing connected transactions in Chapter 14A of
the Listing Rules will not be applicable. Our Directors are of the view that the Technology Licensing
Agreement has been entered into in the ordinary and usual course of business of our Group on normal
commercial terms or better which are fair and reasonable and in the interests of our Company and its
Shareholders as a whole.
Non-exempted Continuing Connected Transactions
As the highest applicable percentage ratio of the three different types of transactions contemplated
under the Product and Service Procurement Framework Agreement for each of the three years ending
December 31, 2028 calculated for the purpose of Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules is expected to exceed
5% on an annual basis, such transactions will, upon Listing, constitute continuing connected transactions
of the Company subject to the annual reporting requirement under Rules 14A.49 and 14A.71 of the Listing
Rules, the announcement requirement under Rule 14A.35 of the Listing Rules and the independent
Shareholders’ approval requirement under Rule 14A.36 of the Listing Rules.
W AIVER APPLICATION FOR NON-EXEMPTED CONTINUING CONNECTED TRANSACTION
By virtue of Rule 14A.76(2) of the Listing Rules, upon Listing, the transactions under the
Non-exempt Continuing Connected Transactions will constitute continuing connected transactions subject
to reporting, annual review, announcement and independent Shareholders’ approval requirements under
Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules.
As the above non-exempt continuing connected transactions are expected to continue on a recurring
and continuing basis, our Directors consider that compliance with the above announcement and/or
independent shareholders’ approval requirements would be impractical, would add unnecessary
administrative costs to us and would be unduly burdensome to us.
Accordingly, we have applied for, and the Stock Exchange [has granted] us, pursuant to Rule
14A.105 of the Listing Rules, waivers from strict compliance with the announcement and independent
Shareholders’ approval requirements under Rule 14A.35 and Rule 14A.36 of the Listing Rules in respect
of these transactions, provided that the total amount of transactions for each of the three years ending
[December 31, 2028] will not exceed the relevant proposed annual caps as set out in this section. Any
material changes to the terms of these continuing connected transactions will be approved by independent
Shareholders. The independent non-executive Directors and auditors of the Company will review annually
whether the transactions under the above continuing connected transactions have been entered into
pursuant to the principal terms and pricing policies under the Product and Service Procurement Framework
Agreement as disclosed in this section pursuant to Rules 14A.55 to 14A.59 of the Listing Rules. The
confirmation from our independent non-executive Directors and our auditors will be disclosed annually
according to the requirements of the Listing Rules.

INTERNAL CONTROL MEASURES

as an independent finance department which makes financial decisions according to our Group’s own
business needs. See “Business — Our Relationship with ECARX Group” and “Relationship with our
Single Largest Group of Shareholders” for further details. In order to ensure that the terms under the
specific agreements to be entered into between Company and the relevant connected persons for the
continuing connected transactions are fair and reasonable, or no less favorable than terms available to or
from Independent Third Parties, and are carried out under normal commercial terms, we will adopt the
following internal control procedures:
 our various internal departments will be responsible for the control and daily management in
respect of the continuing connected transactions;
 our various internal departments will be jointly responsible for evaluating the terms under the
specific agreements for the continuing connected transactions, in particular, the fairness of the
pricing policies and annual caps under each transaction;
 our various internal departments will regularly monitor the fulfillment status of the annual caps
and the transaction updates under the specific agreements to be entered into between Company
and the relevant connected persons; and
 our independent non-executive Directors and auditors will conduct annual review of the
continuing connected transactions under the Product and Service Procurement Framework
Agreement and provide annual confirmation to ensure that, in accordance with the Listing
Rules, the transactions are conducted in accordance with the terms of the Product and Service
Procurement Framework Agreement, on normal commercial terms and in accordance with the
relevant pricing policies.

RESTRICTION ON TRANSFER OF SHARES ISSUED PRIOR TO THE GLOBAL OFFERING
The PRC Company Law provides that in relation to the public share offering of a company, the
shares of the company which have been issued prior to the offering shall not be transferred within one year
from the date of the listing. Accordingly, Shares issued by our Company prior to the Listing Date shall be
subject to this statutory restriction and shall not be transferred for a period of one year from the Listing
Date.
Our Company will work with the Domestic Securities Company to be engaged by our Company to
restrict the trading of the H Shares converted from Unlisted Shares technically within one year after the
Listing.
Pursuant to the PRC Company Law, Shares transferred by our Directors and members of the senior
management each year during their term of office shall not exceed 25% of their total respective
shareholdings in our Company. The Shares that the aforementioned persons held in our Company cannot
be transferred within one year from the date on which the H Shares are listed and traded, nor within half
a year after they leave their positions in our Company. The Articles of Association may contain other
restrictions on the transfer of our Shares held by our Directors and members of senior management, a
summary of which is set out in “Appendix III — Summary of Articles of Association.”

“Appendix III — Summary of Articles of Association.”

BOARD DIVERSITY POLICY
Our Board has adopted a board diversity policy which sets out the approach to achieve diversity on
our Board. Our Company seeks to achieve Board diversity through the consideration of a number of
factors, including but not limited to talent, skills, gender, age, cultural and educational background,
ethnicity, professional experience, independence, knowledge and length of service. We will select
potential Board candidates based on merit and their potential contribution to our Board while taking into
consideration our own business model and specific needs from time to time.
Our Board has a balanced mix
of knowledge, skills and experience. They completed studies in various majors including but without
limitation to communication engineering, automation, economics, and electrical and computer
engineering. We have four independent non-executive Directors who have different industry backgrounds.
Furthermore, our Directors are of a wide range of age, from 37 to 66 years old. Taking into account our
business model and specific needs as well as the presence of two female Directors out of a total of 11
Board members, we consider that the composition of our Board satisfies our board diversity policy.
We recognize the particular importance of gender diversity on our Board. We have taken, and will
continue to take, steps to promote gender diversity at all levels of our Company, including but not limited
to our Board and the senior management levels.
In particular, taking into account the business needs of
our Group and changing circumstances that may affect our business plans, we will actively identify and
select several female individuals with a diverse range of skills, experience and knowledge in different
fields from time to time, and maintain a list of such female individuals who possess qualities to become
our Board members, which will be periodically reviewed by our Nomination Committee in order to
develop a pipeline of potential successors to our Board and promote gender diversity.
We plan to offer
well-rounded trainings to female employees whom we consider have the requisite experience, skills and
knowledge of our operation and business, on topics including but not limited to business operation,
management, accounting and finance, and legal compliance.
After Listing, our Nomination Committee will
review our board diversity policy and its implementation annually to monitor its continued effectiveness .

Shareholders’ meetings and the Board of Directors take into account factors such as salaries paid by
comparable companies, time commitment, level of responsibilities, employment elsewhere in our Group
and desirability of performance-based remuneration. As required by the relevant PRC laws and
regulations, our Company also participates in various defined contribution plans organized by relevant
provincial and municipal government authorities and welfare schemes for employees of our Company,

insurance and housing provident fund.

OVERVIEW
We are a leading domestic provider of high-performance automotive-grade SoCs, delivering
comprehensive automotive intelligence solutions that power key intelligent vehicle functions, from
intelligent cockpit to mid- to high-level advanced driver assistance. Our strategic focus lies in the design
and development of advanced automotive-grade SoCs and solutions.
We have focused on AI-powered
cockpits and the integration of cockpit and driving functionalities. We are the No. 1 domestic supplier in
the automotive SoC market in China in 2025, in terms of installation volume of intelligent cockpit domain
controller SoCs, according to Frost & Sullivan. Leveraging our system-level design approach enabling
unified chip architecture, foundational software platform and comprehensive ecosystem support, we
deliver high-performance automotive-grade SoCs
without compromising on cost or efficiency.
As our SoCs and solutions have been widely deployed and proven reliable under rigorous conditions
of real-world automotive applications, we are helping automotive companies address increasing R&D
complexity, accelerate product innovation, and achieve cost efficiency. As of December 31, 2025, we had
collaborated with prominent domestic automotive OEMs, including Geely, FAW, and Changan, and a
global automotive OEM. Our SoCs have been adopted and deployed by domestic and global vehicle
brands, such as Lynk & Co, Galaxy, Qiyuan, Xingyao , Hong Qi and Proton. As of the Latest Practicable
Date, our SE1000 had been adopted by 30 vehicle models, covering both domestic best-selling models and
global vehicle platforms of international automotive OEMs. According to Frost & Sullivan, nine of these
models that incorporated SE1000 were among the top five best-selling model of their respective brands
in 202
5, such as Galaxy E5, which was the best-selling models for Galaxy in 202 5.
We achieved significant growth during the Track Record Period. Our revenue increased from
RMB110.8 million in 202 3t oR M B 341.8 million in 202 5 at a CAGR of 75.6% . We recorded gross loss
of RMB3.3 million and RMB51.1 million in 2023 and 2024, respectively, representing a gross loss margin
of 3.0% and 21.8% in the same periods, respectively. We recorded gross profit of RMB
38.2 million in
2025, representing a gross profit margin of 11.2% . In 202 5, the shipment volume of SE1000 reached
839,000 units, with cumulative shipments exceeding 1,550,000 units as of December 31, 2025.

MAJOR FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Our results of operations have been, and are expected to continue to be, materially affected by a
number of key factors, including the following:
The Development of and Global Demand for Intelligent Vehicles
Our financial performance is closely tied to the development of the automotive industry in China and
globally, particularly the fast-growing intelligent vehicle segment. The overall demand for automobiles is
the primary driver of our business performance, which is influenced by macroeconomic cycles, consumer
sentiment, and the stability of global supply chains. In recent years, fueled by the accelerating adoption
of electrification and advanced vehicle intelligence, the automotive industry has been undergoing a
profound transformation. Consumers are increasingly seeking vehicles that deliver safer, more
comfortable and more personalized driving experiences — demands that traditional vehicles without
intelligent features can no longer satisfy. In response, automotive OEMs are placing heightened emphasis
on integrating intelligent functions, including advanced driver assistance, automated parking, voice
interaction, and immersive infotainment systems, which have emerged as pivotal differentiators within the
automotive industry. These intelligent features, once exclusive to premium models, are now being
adopted
across vehicles of all price segments, fueling sustained demand for automotive-grade SoCs, with growth
observed in the markets for intelligent cockpit SoCs and ADAS SoCs. According to Frost & Sullivan, the
global automotive intelligent cockpit SoC market is projected to grow from RMB 45.9 billion in 202 6t o
RMB94.0 billion in 20 30 at a CAGR of 19.6%. The global autonomous driving SoC market is projected
to grow from RMB 82.1 billion in 2026 to reach RMB 161.0 billion in 2029 at a CAGR of 18.3%.
Meanwhile, domestic substitution is a critical trend in China’s automotive SoC market. According
to Frost & Sullivan, the market for China’s automotive intelligent cockpit SoC market is projected to reach
RMB42.8 billion in 20 30 at a CAGR of 15.2% from 2026 to 2030. China’s autonomous driving SoC
market is projected to reach RMB 82.0 billion in 20 30 at a CAGR of 18.3% from 2026 to 2030. According
to Frost & Sullivan, the adoption rate of domestic intelligent cockpit SoCs is expected to rise from
approximately 12% in 2024 to 40% by 2029, while the adoption rate of domestic ADAS SoCs is projected
to increase from approximately 19% in 2024 to 45% by 2029. The growth of the automotive SoC market
and our ability to capitalize on these opportunities are vital for our future revenue scale and growth rate.

Our Ability to Commercialize Our Products and Maintain Technology Leadership
Our competitive advantage stems from our established technology leadership and sustained
innovation in automotive-grade SoCs and solutions. We have built a full-scenario portfolio of
automotive-grade high-performance SoCs, based on which we offer solutions covering applications from
intelligent cockpit to ADAS. In
2023, 2024 and 2025, revenue from the sales of SoCs and solutions
amounted to RMB110.8 million, RMB234.5 million and RMB 341.8 million, respectively.
Our revenue growth depends on our ability to commercialize our existing products and solutions, as
well as to develop new and enhanced offerings. The significant revenue growth during the Track Record
Period was mainly driven by the successful mass production and rapid market adoption of SE1000 of our
StarEagle series, China’s first 7nm automotive-grade intelligent cockpit SoC. Since the mass production
of SE1000 in 2023, the shipment volume of SE1000 increased from 173,000 units in 2023 to 541,000 units
in 2024, and
further to 839,000 units in 2025. In addition to our intelligent cockpit SoCs, we launched
industrial-grade SoCs in July 2024, ADAS SoCs in March 2025, and AI accelerator SoCs in April 2025.
Among these, our ADAS SoC, AD1000 of the StarLight series became eligible for mass production in
December 2025. By effectively commercializing and expanding our product offerings, we believe we can
maintain our competitive edge in the market while fostering sustained growth.
Continued investment in R&D is essential to sustaining our competitive edge. We incurred research
and development expenses of
RMB594.5 million, RMB583.2 million and RMB 584.1 million in 2023,
2024 and 2025, respectively, accounting for 536.6%, 248.7% and 170.9% of our total revenue in the same
periods, respectively. We are firmly committed to sustained investment in research and development,
which we believe is instrumental in fortifying our technological barriers and reinforcing our market
position, thereby supporting sustainable business growth. While, such investments will lead to an increase
in our research and development expenses in absolute amounts, potentially impacting our results of
operations and financial condition in the short term, we expect that as our business scales and R&D
efficiency improves, our research and development expenses as a percentage of revenue will decrease.
Our Ability to Broaden Adoption among Automotive OEMs and Tier-One Suppliers
Our business growth depends significantly on our ability to broaden the adoption of our products
among automotive OEMs and tier-one suppliers. Automotive OEMs determine vehicle-level technology
roadmaps, platform specifications, and sourcing decisions, and their selection of our products and
solutions directly influences the scale and longevity of the adoption of our SoCs across multiple vehicle
models. As of
December 31, 2025, we had collaborated with prominent domestic automotive companies
such as Geely, FAW, and Changan, and a global automotive OEM. We also provide SoCs and solutions to
tier-one suppliers for the integration into their domain controllers and other advanced system-level
solutions. Driven by the extended vehicle platform cycles, recurring demand throughout each vehicle’s
production lifecycle, and our ability to seamlessly scale solutions across successive platform generations,
broader adoption by automotive OEMs and tier-one suppliers will enable us to achieve greater revenue
visibility, stronger margins, and sustained business growth.
To further strengthen adoption among our existing automotive OEM and tier-one customers, we plan
to (i) deepen joint product planning to align future SoC roadmaps with their evolving technology
architectures; (ii) broaden and strengthen our technical collaboration by engaging in co-development
initiatives, providing comprehensive application engineering support, and accelerating validation cycles to
ensure rapid and effective product deployment and adoption; and (iii) enhance our software, toolchain and
reference design offerings to improve integration efficiency and reduce time-to-production for existing
customer programs.
We also intend to broaden our customer base by (i) expanding our SoC portfolio and introducing
more SoC variants to address a wider range of vehicle platform requirements; (ii) improving integration

Our Ability to Control Costs and Optimize Operational Efficiency
Under our fabless business model, the manufacturing, assembly and testing of our SoCs are
conducted by contract manufacturers and OSA T service providers. During the initial commercialization
phase of our SE1000, Supplier C assisted us in coordinating with Supplier F and OSA T service providers
in connection with the production of our SoCs. Starting from 2024, we gradually transitioned to engaging
directly with contract manufacturer and OSA T service providers as we strengthened our supply chain
management, which facilitated better cost control and contributed to an improved gross margin profile. For
details, see “Business — Suppliers — Our Major Suppliers.” In
2023, 2024 and 2025, our cost of inventory
sold, primarily comprising cost of raw materials and contract manufacturing, assembly and testing
services, amounted to
RMB99.9 million, RMB259.8 million and RMB 270.0 million, respectively,
accounting for 87.5%, 90.9% and 89.0% of our total cost of revenue in the same periods, respectively.
Supply chain management and stability are critical for fabless semiconductor companies like us, as we
engage third-party foundry, OSA T service providers, and other upstream partners for timely and reliable
production. To enhance the continuity and resilience of our supply chain, we plan to implement a
multi-vendor strategy by diversifying chip manufacturing suppliers across multiple regions. We also
maintain appropriate inventory stock and adjust production planning based on demand forecasts and
market conditions to mitigate potential disruptions.
Our ability to manage and control our operating expenses is also critical to the success of our
business. During the Track Record Period, we incurred substantial general and administrative expenses of
RMB112.5 million, RMB108.0 million and RMB 142.5 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively,
accounting for 101.5%, 46.0% and 41.7% of our total revenue in the same periods, respectively. Our
selling and marketing expenses also increased from RMB14.9 million in 2023 to RMB15.0 million in 2024
and further to RMB 18.1 million in 2025, primarily due to our commitment to increasing our sales and
marketing capabilities , accounting for 13.4%, 6.4% and 5.3% of our total revenue in the same periods,
respectively. As we expand our business, improve our operating efficiency and benefit from economies of
scale, we expect our operating expenses to decrease as a percentage of our total revenue.
Seasonality
Demand for our SoCs demonstrates a clear seasonal pattern primarily driven by the production and
sales cycles of automotive OEMs. In the first quarter of each year, automotive OEMs typically reduce
production volume due to the Chinese New Y ear holidays and the accompanying slowdown in dealer
sell-through, which in turn reduces their procurement activities for automotive components, including
SoCs. Procurement of automotive SoCs tends to pick up in the second half of the year, most notably in
the fourth quarter, as automotive OEMs ramp up vehicle production to meet year-end sales targets, support
model-year changeovers and secure sufficient component inventories ahead of the holiday season.
Correspondingly, our licensing and development services, which include licensing of our foundational
software platform as well as customization and adaptation support, are primarily delivered in the fourth
quarter. As a result, our sales are generally concentrated in the fourth quarter, reflecting the heightened
production planning and inventory stocking requirements of automotive OEMs during this period. These
seasonal dynamics are consistent with broader patterns in the Chinese automotive market.

During the Track Record Period, the gross margin of our intelligent cockpit SoCs and solutions
fluctuated. With the commencement of the mass production of our SE1000 in March 2023, we entered a
production ramp-up phase. Despite the corresponding increase in customer demand for our licensing and
development services as well as technical support services, both of which yielded relatively high gross
margins, we recorded a gross loss margin of 3.0% in 2023 due to the initial costs and operational
adjustments required for scaling manufacturing. Our gross loss margin increased to 21.8% in 2024,
primarily due to (i) a shift in revenue mix, as a result of the increase in revenue contribution from SE1000,
which remained in a gross loss position because of our early-stage supply chain arrangements to accelerate
time to market; and (ii) our dynamic pricing and marketing strategy implemented to promote our product
sales, expand our market share and further enhance our customer relationship.
In 2025, however, we
recorded a gross profit margin of 11.2%, driven by (i) the optimization of our supply chain management,
whereby we directly procured wafers and OSA T services to facilitate our cost control, and introduced
suppliers offering more favorable commercial terms; (ii) the economies of scale achieved through
increased procurement and production volumes, as well as improved manufacturing processes ; (iii) the
optimization of testing procedures and improvements in yield rates; and (iv) the increase in revenue
contribution from services with a higher profit margin.
Our sales of industrial-grade SoCs and solutions primarily comprised sample sales during the Track
Record Period. Therefore, the gross margins of our industrial-grade SoCs and solutions during the Track
Record Period were not indicative of the margins that may be achieved upon large-scale delivery to
customers.
Our sales of ADAS SoCs and solutions and AI accelerator SoCs and solutions in 2025 comprised of
software licensing arrangements in respect of software developed through our R&D efforts, which did not
incur any direct operating costs. Accordingly, the gross profit margins of our ADAS SoCs and solutions
and AI accelerator SoCs and solutions were 100% and were not indicative of the gross margin that may
be achieved upon large-scale commercial delivery of such SoCs to customers in the future.

Income Tax
Pursuant to the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the PRC (the “ EIT Law ”), our Company and
subsidiaries established and operating in the PRC are subject to an enterprise income tax at a rate of 25%
unless otherwise specified. In accordance with the EIT Law and its relevant regulations, our Company was
recognized as a High and New-Technology Enterprise and enjoyed a preferential tax rate of 15% during
the Track Record Period. In addition, certain of our subsidiaries qualified as
small- size minimal profit
enterprise were entitled to a preferential tax treatment of 75% exemption of taxable income and an income
tax rate of 20% during the Track Record Period.
We did not incur income tax in 2023 and 2024, due to our loss positions. In 2025, we recorded
income tax of RMB2.0 million, which was primarily attributable to withholding income tax in respect of
revenue of RMB20.0 million generated from overseas. During the Track Record Period and up to the
Latest Practicable Date, we had paid all relevant taxes when due and there were no matters in dispute or
unresolved with the relevant tax authorities.

arrangements to accelerate time to market; and (ii) our dynamic pricing and marketing strategy
implemented to promote our product adoption, expand our market share and further enhance our customer
relationship.
Research and Development Expenses
Our research and development expenses slightly decreased from RMB594.5 million in 2023 to
RMB583.2 million in 2024, primarily due to the improvement in our R&D efficiency, as evidenced by the
one-time tape-out of our AD1000.
Selling and Marketing Expenses
Our selling and marketing expenses remained relatively stable at RMB14.9 million and RMB15.0
million in 2023 and 2024, respectively.

STABILIZATION ACTION
Stabilization is a practice used by underwriters in some markets to facilitate the distribution of
securities. To stabilize, the Underwriters may bid for, or purchase, the securities in the secondary market,
during a specified period of time, to retard and, if possible, prevent a decline in the initial public market
price of the securities below the offer price. Such transactions may be effected in all jurisdictions where
it is permissible to do so, in each case in compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements,
including those of Hong Kong. In Hong Kong, the price at which stabilization is effected is not permitted
to exceed the offer price.
In connection with the Global Offering, the Stabilizing Manager (or its affiliates or any person acting
for it), on behalf of the Underwriters, may over-allocate or effect transactions with a view to stabilizing
or maintaining the market price of our H Shares at a level higher than that which might otherwise prevail
in the open market for a limited period after the Listing Date. However, there is no obligation on the
Stabilizing Manager (or its affiliates or any person acting for it) to conduct any such stabilizing action.
Such stabilizing action, if taken, (a) will be conducted at the absolute discretion of the Stabilizing Manager
(or its affiliates or any person acting for it) and in what the Stabilization Manager reasonably regards as
the best interest of the Company, (b) may be discontinued at any time, and (c) is required to be brought
to an end within 30 days of the last day for lodging applications under the Hong Kong Public Offering.

Stabilization action permitted in Hong Kong under the Securities and Futures (Price Stabilizing)
Rules of the SFO includes (i) over-allocating for the purpose of preventing or minimizing any reduction
in the market price of our H Shares, (ii) selling or agreeing to sell our H Shares so as to establish a short
position in them for the purpose of preventing or minimizing any reduction in the market price of our H
Shares, (iii) purchasing, or agreeing to purchase, our H Shares pursuant to the Over-Allotment Option in
order to close out any position established under (i) or (ii) above, (iv) purchasing, or agreeing to purchase,
any of our H Shares for the sole purpose of preventing or minimizing any reduction in the market price
of our H Shares, (v) selling or agreeing to sell any H Shares in order to liquidate any position established
as a result of those purchases, and (vi) offering or attempting to do anything as described in (ii), (iii), (iv)
or (v) above.
Specifically, prospective applicants for and investors in H Shares should note that:
 the Stabilizing Manager (or its affiliates or any person acting for it) may, in connection with
the stabilizing action, maintain a long position in the H Shares;
 there is no certainty as to the extent to which and the time or period for which the Stabilizing
Manager (or its affiliates or any person acting for it) will maintain such a long position;
 liquidation of any such long position by the Stabilizing Manager (or its affiliates or any person
acting for it) and selling in the open market may have an adverse impact on the market price
of the H Shares;
 no stabilizing action can be taken to support the price of the H Shares for longer than the
stabilizing period, which will begin on the Listing Date and is expected to expire on
October
25, 2026, being the 30th day after the last day for lodging applications under the Hong Kong
Public Offering. After this date, when no further action may be taken to support the price of
the H Shares, demand for the H Shares, and therefore the price of the H Shares, could fall;
 the price of the H Shares cannot be assured to stay at or above the Offer Price by the taking
of any stabilizing action; and
 stabilizing bids or transactions effected in the course of the stabilizing action may be made at
any price at or below the Offer Price, which means that stabilizing bids or transactions effected
may be made at a price below the price paid by applicants for, or investors in, the Offer Shares.
In order to effect stabilization actions, the Stabilizing Manager will cover up to an aggregate of
7,319,900 H Shares, representing up to 15% of the initial Offer Shares, through delayed delivery
arrangements with investors who have been allocated Offer Shares in the International Offering. The
delayed delivery arrangements (if specifically agreed by an investor) relate only to the delay in the
delivery of the Offer Shares to such investor and the consideration for the Offer Shares allocated to such
investor will be settled before the Listing Date. Both the size of such cover and the extent to which the
Over-Allotment Option can be exercised will depend on whether arrangements can be made with investors
such that a sufficient number of H Shares can be delivered on a delayed basis. If no investor in the
International Offering agrees to the delayed delivery arrangements, no stabilizing actions will be
undertaken by the Stabilizing Manager and the Over-Allotment Option will not be exercised.
The Company will ensure or procure that an announcement in compliance with the Securities and
Futures (Price Stabilizing) Rules of the SFO will be made within seven days of the expiration of the
stabilization period.

1 BASIS OF PREPARATION AND PRESENTATION OF HISTORICAL FINANCIAL
INFORMATION
SiEngine Technology Co., Ltd.ʮ̡ (the “Company”), formerly known as ಳ
ʮ̡, was incorporated in the People’s Republic of China (the “PRC”) on 18 September
2018 as a limited liability company under the Company Law of the PRC. In December 2025, the Company
was converted from a limited liability company into a joint stock limited liability company.
During the Relevant Periods, the Company and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as “the
Group”) are primarily engaged in design, research and development and sale of automotive (including
intelligent cockpit and autonomous driving (“AD”)) and industrial-grade system on chip (“SoC”) products
and provision of SoC-based solutions and services. The Group’s principal operations are in the PRC.
The Historical Financial Information has been prepared assuming the Group will continue as a going
concern notwithstanding the net liabilities of the Group of
RMB3,653,468,000 and net current liabilities
of the Group of RMB3,997,201,000 as at 31 December 2025, primarily due to the redemption liabilities
of RMB3, 745,951,000 (Note 24). The directors of the Company expect no cash payment for the settlement
of the redemption liabilities on or before the original qualified IPO date of 31 December 2026 on the basis
that 1) the redemption rights were conditionally terminated on 28 December 2025 and would only be
resumed upon the occurrence or non-occurrence of certain events, including but not limited to the
non-completion of IPO within 24 months from the dates of the supplemental agreements entered into
between the Company and the investors in October and December 2025 (Note 24); and 2) the redemption
liabilities would be converted into equity upon completion of the IPO.
The Group has unutilized banking
facilities of RMB230,000,000 as at 31 December 2025, which can be utilized by the Group to fulfil its
liquidity requirements when necessary; and the Directors have reviewed the Group’s cash flow
projections, which cover a period of more than twelve months from 31 December 2025 and are of the
opinion that the Group will have sufficient working capital to meet its liabilities and obligations as and
when they fall due and to sustain its operations for at least the next twelve months from 31 December
2025. Accordingly, the directors of the Company consider it is appropriate to prepare the Historical
Financial Information on a going concern basis.
The Historical Financial Information has been prepared in accordance with all applicable IFRS

are not yet effective for the Relevant Periods. The revised and new accounting standards and
