Rules.
The Company shall establish a director resignation management system. When a director’s
resignation takes effect or the director’s term expires, the director shall complete all handover procedures
with the Board of Directors. The duties of loyalty owed to the Company and its shareholders do not
automatically cease upon the end of the term and remain effective within a reasonable period as stipulated
in the Articles of Association. Liabilities arising from the performance of duties during the director’s term
shall not be exempted or terminated by their departure.
The shareholders’ meeting may resolve to remove a director, and such removal shall take effect on
the date the resolution is made.
Unless provided in the Articles of Association or legally authorised by the Board of Directors, no
director shall act on behalf of the Company or the Board of Directors in a personal capacity. When a
director acts in a personal capacity but a third party reasonably believes the director is acting on behalf
of the Company or the Board of Directors, the director shall declare their position and capacity in advance.
If a director, in performing duties, causes damage to others, the Company shall bear compensation
liability; if the director acts with intent or gross negligence, the director shall also be liable for
compensation.
If a director, in performing duties, violates laws, administrative regulations, departmental rules, the
Hong Kong Listing Rules, the securities regulatory rules of the Company’s stock listing place, provisions
of relevant regulatory authorities, or the Articles of Association, and causes losses to the Company, the
director shall be liable for compensation.
The Company shall appoint independent non-executive directors. Independent non-executive
directors shall perform their duties in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, the Hong Kong Listing
Rules, and the Articles of Association.
The Board of Directors
The Company shall establish a Board of Directors, which shall consist of eleven directors. The
directors are classified into executive directors, non-executive directors, and independent non-executive
directors, including four independent non-executive directors. The Board shall have a Chairman and a
Co-Chairman.
The Board of Directors shall exercise the following powers:
(i) Convene shareholders’ meetings and report to the shareholders’ meeting;
(ii) Implement resolutions of the shareholders’ meeting;
(iii) Decide on the Company’s business plans and investment proposals;
(iv) Formulate the Company’s profit distribution plans and loss recovery plans;

The Board of Directors shall explain to the shareholders’ meeting any modified audit opinions issued
by the certified public accountants regarding the Company’s financial reports.
The Board shall formulate the rules of procedure for the Board to ensure implementation of the
shareholders’ meeting’s resolutions by the Board, improve work efficiency, and guarantee scientific
decision-making. The rules of procedure for the Board shall be appended to the Articles of Association,
drafted by the Board and implemented upon approval by the shareholders’ meeting.
The Board shall have a Chairman and a Co-Chairman. The Chairman and Co-Chairman shall be
elected and removed by a majority of all directors. The term of office of the Chairman and Co-Chairman
shall be three years, and they may be re-elected. The Chairman shall exercise the following powers:
(i) Preside over shareholders’ meetings and convene and preside over Board meetings;
(ii) Supervise and inspect the implementation of Board resolutions;
(iii) Sign the Company’s shares, corporate bonds, and other securities;
(iv) Sign important Board documents and other documents requiring the legal representative’s
signature;
(v) Exercise special disposal powers for Company affairs in emergencies caused by major natural
disasters or other force majeure events, in compliance with laws and regulations and in the
interests of the Company, and report to the Board and the shareholders’ meeting afterwards;
(vi) Other powers delegated by the Board;
(vii) Other powers prescribed by laws, administrative regulations, departmental rules, the Hong
Kong Listing Rules, the securities regulatory rules of the Company’s stock listing place,
requirements of relevant regulatory authorities, or the Articles of Association.
If the Chairman is unable or fails to perform his/her duties, the Co-Chairman shall perform the
duties. If the Co-Chairman is unable or fails to perform his/her duties, a director elected jointly by a
majority of the directors shall perform the duties.
Board meetings shall be classified into regular meetings and extraordinary meetings. Regular
meetings shall be held at least four times a year, generally once per quarter.
An extraordinary Board meeting may be proposed by shareholders representing more than one-tenth
of the voting rights, more than one-third of the directors, or the Audit Committee. The Chairman shall
convene and preside over the meeting within ten days of receiving the proposal.
Notice for regular Board meetings shall be given in writing at least 14 days in advance; notice for
extraordinary Board meetings shall be given in writing at least five days in advance. The Board may, based
on circumstances, waive the aforementioned notice periods. Any director present at the meeting shall be
deemed to have received due notice thereof, provided that no objection regarding the lack of notice is
raised at or prior to the commencement of the meeting.

The notice of a Board meeting shall include:
(i) Date and venue of the meeting;
(ii) Duration of the meeting;
(iii) Matters and agenda;
(iv) Date of issuance of the notice.
A Board meeting may only be held with a quorum of more than half of the directors present.
Resolutions of the Board must be passed by a majority of all directors.
V oting on Board resolutions shall be conducted on a one director, one vote basis.
If a director has a connected relationship with an enterprise or individual involved in a Board
resolution, the director shall promptly report the information in writing to the Board. A connected director
shall not vote on the resolution or vote by proxy for another director. The Board meeting may proceed with
a quorum of more than half of the non-connected directors, and resolutions shall be passed by a majority
of the non-connected directors. If fewer than three non-connected directors are present, the matter shall
be submitted to the shareholders’ meeting for approval.
Board meetings may be held in person, by written resolutions circulated for signature, or by other
means approved by all directors. If a Board meeting is held in person, directors may participate via
telephone, video, or other means to facilitate attendance. A director attending by telephone, video or other
means shall be deemed present at the in-person meeting.
If a major shareholder (defined in this section as a shareholder individually or collectively holding
more than 10% of the Company’s shares carrying voting rights) or director has a significant conflict of
interest in matters to be considered by the Board, such matters shall be handled by convening a Board
meeting rather than by written resolutions. Independent non-executive directors who, along with their
close associates (as defined under the Hong Kong Listing Rules), have no material interest in the
transaction shall attend the relevant Board meeting.
If the Board expects to decide on the declaration, recommendation, or payment of dividends, or to
approve any announcement of profits or losses for any annual, semi-annual, or other period at a
forthcoming meeting, an announcement must be issued in compliance with the requirements of the Hong
Kong Listing Rules at least seven working days prior to such meeting.
V oting at Board meetings shall be conducted by way of a poll.
Extraordinary Board meetings may be held and resolutions be made by correspondence, provided
that all directors are afforded a full opportunity to express their views. Any resolution so passed shall be
signed by all participating directors.
Directors shall attend Board meetings in person. If unable to attend, a director may authorise another
director in writing to attend as a proxy. The power of attorney shall specify the proxy’s name, matters
entrusted, scope of authorisation, and validity period, and be signed or sealed by the director. The proxy
shall exercise rights within the authorised scope. Directors not attending a Board meeting and not
authorising a proxy to attend shall be deemed to have waived voting rights for that meeting.
The Board shall prepare minutes of the decisions made at the meeting, with designated personnel
responsible for the minutes, and the minutes shall be signed by all directors present at the meeting.

Independent Non-executive Directors
Independent non-executive directors shall conscientiously perform their duties, play a role in
decision-making, supervision, checks and balances, and professional consultation within the Board of
Directors, safeguarding the overall interests of the Company and protecting the lawful rights and interests
of minority shareholders, in compliance with laws, administrative regulations, the Hong Kong Listing
Rules, the securities regulatory rules of the Company’s stock listing place, provisions of relevant
regulatory authorities, the Articles of Association, and the Company’s current Rules of Work for
Independent Non-Executive Directors.
Independent non-executive directors must possess independence in accordance with the Hong Kong
Listing Rules. They shall conduct a self-assessment of their independence annually and submit the results
to the Board. The Board shall assess the independence of incumbent independent non-executive directors
annually and issue a special opinion, which shall be disclosed simultaneously with the annual report.
Except for cases exempted by the stock exchange of the listing place, candidates for independent
non-executive director generally shall not be subject to the following circumstances; otherwise, their
independence is likely to be questioned by the stock exchange:
(i) The person holds more than 1% of the Company’s issued shares;
(ii) The person has received any securities interest from the Company or its core connected persons
in the form of gifts or other financial support, except for securities interest acquired as part of
director remuneration or under a share scheme;
(iii) The person is or was a director, partner, or principal of a professional adviser that is providing,
or within the two years prior to the proposed appointment, provided services to the following
companies/persons, or is or was an employee of such professional adviser who participates or

Specialised Committees under the Board
The Company’s Board of Directors shall establish audit, strategy, nomination, and remuneration and
appraisal committees, as well as other specialised committees, to perform their duties in accordance with
the Articles of Association and the authority delegated by the Board. Proposals from these committees
shall be submitted to the Board for deliberation and decision. The working rules of the committees shall
be formulated by the Board.
The Board shall establish an Audit Committee, which shall exercise the powers of the supervisory
board under the Company Law. The Audit Committee shall comprise at least three directors, all of whom
must be non-executive directors. At least one member of the Audit Committee shall be an independent
non-executive director with appropriate professional qualifications recognised by the listing rules of the
stock exchange of the Company’s listing place or with appropriate accounting or related financial
management expertise, and the majority of the Audit Committee members, including the chair (convener),
shall be independent non-executive directors. Any former partner of the Company’s current external audit
firm shall not serve as a member of the Audit Committee within two years from the later of (i) the date
he/she ceased to be a partner of that firm, or (ii) the date he/she ceased to have any financial interest in
that firm.

SENIOR MANAGEMENT
The Company shall have one general manager, appointed or dismissed by the Board of Directors.
The chief financial officer and head of R&D shall be nominated by the general manager and
appointed by the Board of Directors.
The provisions of the Articles of Association regarding the circumstances under which a person may
not serve as a director as well as the resignation management system shall also apply to senior
management. Any appointment of senior management in violation of the provisions of the Articles of
Association shall be null and void. If such circumstances arise during the term of a senior management
member, the Company shall dismiss the senior management member from his/her position and suspend
his/her duties.
The provisions of the Articles of Association regarding the duties of loyalty and diligence of
directors shall also apply to senior management.
The term of the general manager shall be three years. The general manager may be reappointed for
consecutive terms.
The general manager shall be accountable to the Board of Directors and shall exercise the following
powers:
(i) Preside over the Company’s production, operation, and management activities, implement the
resolutions of the Board of Directors, and report to the Board of Directors;
(ii) Implement the Company’s annual business plans and investment proposals;
(iii) Draft proposals for the establishment of the Company’s internal management structure;
(iv) Draft the Company’s basic management systems;
(v) Formulate the Company’s specific regulations;
(vi) Propose to the Board of Directors the appointment or dismissal of the chief financial officer
and head of R&D;
(vii) Decide on the appointment or dismissal of management personnel other than those whose
appointment or dismissal is to be decided by the Board of Directors;
(viii) Other powers not conferred on the shareholders’ meeting or the Board by laws, administrative
regulations, departmental rules, the Hong Kong Listing Rules, the securities regulatory rules of
the Company’s stock listing place, requirements of relevant regulatory authorities, or the
Articles of Association;
(ix) Other powers granted by the Articles of Association, or the Board of Directors.
The general manager may attend Board meetings as a non-voting participant.
The general manager shall formulate the rules of work, which shall be implemented upon approval
by the Board of Directors.

FINANCIAL AND ACCOUNTING SYSTEM
The Company shall establish its financial and accounting system in accordance with laws,
administrative regulations, and provisions of relevant national authorities.
The Company’s financial year shall follow the Gregorian calendar, from January 1 to December 31.
The Company shall prepare annual financial accounting reports within four (4) months after the end of
each financial year in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, the Hong Kong Listing Rules, the
securities regulatory rules of the Company’s stock listing place, and requirements of relevant regulatory
authorities. The Company shall prepare interim financial accounting reports within two (2) months after
the end of the first six months of each financial year.
The Company shall not establish separate accounting books in addition to the statutory accounting
books. The Company’s assets shall not be stored in accounts opened in the name of any individual.
When distributing the after-tax profits of the current year, the Company shall allocate 10% of the
profits to the Company’s statutory reserve fund. If the cumulative amount of the Company’s statutory
reserve fund exceeds 50% of the Company’s registered capital, the Company may cease to make further
allocations.
If the Company’s statutory reserve fund is insufficient to cover the losses of previous years, the
Company shall use the current year’s profits to cover the losses before allocating the statutory reserve fund
as stipulated above.
After allocating the statutory reserve fund from the after-tax profits, the Company may also allocate
a discretionary reserve fund from the after-tax profits upon a resolution of the shareholders’ meeting.

After covering losses and allocating reserve funds, the remaining after-tax profits shall be distributed

If the shareholders’ meeting distributes profits to shareholders in violation of the Company Law, the
shareholders shall return the improperly distributed profits to the Company; shareholders, as well as the
responsible directors and senior management members, shall bear liability for any resulting losses caused
to the Company.
Shares of the Company held by the Company itself shall not participate in profit distribution.
The Company implements a continuous and stable profit distribution policy. The specific method of
profit distribution shall be determined in light of the Company’s profit performance, cash flow situation,
and capital scale.
Profit distribution may be made in cash, in shares, in a combination of cash and shares, or by other
means permitted by laws and regulations. Where conditions for cash dividends are met, the Company
shall, in principle, give priority to distributing profits in cash.
The Company’s reserve funds shall be used to cover the Company’s losses, expand its production and
operations, or increase its registered capital.
When reserve funds are used to cover losses, the discretionary reserve fund and the statutory reserve
fund shall be used first; if the losses cannot be fully covered, the capital reserve fund may be used in
accordance with regulations.
When the statutory reserve fund is converted into registered capital, the retained statutory reserve
fund shall not be less than 25% of the Company’s registered capital before the conversion.
The Company’s profit distribution plan shall be proposed by the Board of Directors. After the
shareholders’ meeting resolves on the profit distribution plan, the Board of Directors shall complete the
distribution of dividends (or shares) within two months following the meeting.
After paying income tax and making up any losses from the previous year, the Company’s profits
shall be distributed in the following order:
(i) Appropriation to the statutory reserve fund;
(ii) Appropriation to the discretionary reserve fund as resolved by the shareholders’ meeting;
(iii) Payment of dividends to shareholders as resolved by the shareholders’ meeting.
The Company shall appoint receiving agents for holders of overseas-listed foreign shares. Such
agents shall, on behalf of these shareholders, collect and hold dividends and other amounts payable by the
Company in respect of the overseas-listed foreign shares, pending payment to the shareholders.
The receiving agents appointed by the Company shall comply with relevant laws of the stock listing
place or regulations of the stock exchange.

DISSOLUTION AND LIQUIDATION
The Company may be dissolved for the following reasons:
(i) The business term stipulated in the Articles of Association expires or other dissolution causes
stipulated in the Articles of Association arise;
(ii) The shareholders’ meeting resolves to dissolve the Company;
(iii) The Company needs to be dissolved due to a merger or division;
(iv) The Company has its business licence revoked, is ordered to close down, or is dissolved by
competent authorities;
(v) The Company’s operation and management encounter serious difficulties, and its continued
existence would cause significant losses to shareholders’ interests, and no other solutions can
be found. Shareholders holding more than 10% of the Company’s voting rights may request the
People’s Court to dissolve the Company.
When the Company encounters any of the dissolution causes mentioned above, it shall publicise the
dissolution causes through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System within ten days.
If the Company encounters the circumstances mentioned in items (i) and (ii) above and has not yet
distributed its assets to shareholders, it may continue to exist by amending its Articles of Association or
by a resolution of the shareholders’ meeting.
Such an amendment or resolution requires approval by more than two-thirds of the voting rights held
by shareholders present at the shareholders’ meeting.
If the Company is dissolved due to the circumstances mentioned in items (i), (ii), (iv), and (v) above,
it shall be liquidated. The directors shall serve as the liquidation obligors and establish a liquidation team
within 15 days from the date the dissolution cause arises to commence liquidation.
The liquidation team shall consist of directors, unless the Articles of Association provides otherwise
or the shareholders’ meeting resolves to appoint others.
If the liquidation obligors fail to perform their liquidation obligations in a timely manner, causing
losses to the Company or creditors, they shall bear the liability for compensation.
During the liquidation period, the liquidation team shall exercise the following powers:
(i) Liquidate the Company’s assets and preparing a balance sheet and a property inventory
separately;
(ii) Notify and announce to creditors;
(iii) Handle the Company’s unfinished business related to the liquidation;
(iv) Pay off the taxes owed and the taxes incurred during the liquidation process;
(v) Settle claims and debts;

The liquidation team shall, within ten days of its establishment, notify the creditors, and within 60
days, make an announcement in the designated newspaper (or the National Enterprise Credit Information
Publicity System), and make an announcement on the HKEXnews website (http://www.hkexnews.hk) in
accordance with the securities regulatory rules of the Company’s stock listing place. Creditors shall
declare their claims to the liquidation team within 30 days from the date of receiving the notice or within
45 days from the date of the announcement if they have not received the notice.
When declaring claims, creditors shall explain the relevant matters of the claims and provide
supporting materials. The liquidation team shall register the claims.
During the claim declaration period, the liquidation team shall not settle claims with creditors.
After liquidating the Company’s assets and preparing a balance sheet and a property inventory, the
liquidation team shall formulate a liquidation plan and submit it to the shareholders’ meeting or the
People’s Court for confirmation.
After paying the liquidation expenses, employees’ wages, social insurance contributions and
statutory compensation, settling the taxes owed, and repaying the Company’s debts, the remaining assets
of the Company shall be distributed to the shareholders in proportion to their shareholdings.
During the liquidation period, the Company shall continue to exist but shall not engage in business
activities unrelated to the liquidation.
The Company’s assets shall not be distributed to shareholders before being settled in accordance with
the preceding paragraph.
After liquidating the Company’s assets and preparing a balance sheet and a property inventory, if the
liquidation team finds that the Company’s assets are insufficient to settle its debts, it shall apply to the
People’s Court for bankruptcy liquidation in accordance with the law.
After the People’s Court accepts the bankruptcy application, the liquidation team shall transfer the
liquidation matters to the bankruptcy administrator designated by the People’s Court.
After the Company’s liquidation is completed, the liquidation team shall prepare a liquidation report,
submit it to the shareholders’ meeting or the People’s Court for confirmation, and submit it to the company
registration authority to apply for cancellation of the Company’s registration.
Members of the liquidation team shall perform their liquidation duties with loyalty and diligence.
Members of the liquidation team who neglect to perform their liquidation duties and cause losses to
the Company shall be liable for compensation; if losses are caused to creditors due to intentional
misconduct or gross negligence, they shall be liable for compensation.
If the Company is legally declared bankrupt, it shall implement bankruptcy liquidation in accordance
with relevant enterprise bankruptcy laws.

Participant.

partnerships, shall subscribe for the capital contribution of the limited partnership interest, by methods as
stipulated in the Share Incentive Plans, thereby indirectly holding the Shares of our Company by virtue
of their capacity as a partner of the relevant Incentive Platform.

The lock-up period for Incentive Awards shall commence from date of the grant and to the date (i)
the date falling 12 months after the listing of the Company’s shares on a recognized stock exchange; and
(ii) the date on which the Participant has accumulated three years of employment with the Group, which
occurs later. During the lock-up period, the partnership interests shall not be transferred, pledged, assigned
or disposed, unless with the prior consent of Dr. Wang Kai.

7. Repurchase and Forfeiture of Incentive Interests
Where, during the lock-up period, the employment relationship between a Participant and our Group
is terminated or ceases for any reason, or where such employment relationship has not been terminated but
the Participant is determined to be unable to perform, or is no longer suitable to continue performing, his
or her original duties, each of the Incentive Platforms shall have the right to repurchase all or part of the
incentive interests held by such Participant, and such Participant shall withdraw accordingly. In such
event, each of the Incentive Platforms shall refund to the relevant Participant the corresponding amount
of capital actually contributed by such Participant.
Where any of the following events occurs, whether during or after the lock-up period, each of the
Incentive Platforms shall have the right to forfeit, without consideration, the relevant Participant’s
incentive interests and any distributable profits therefrom, and shall not refund any capital contribution
made by such Participant, and such Participant shall withdraw accordingly:
(i) the Participant fails to continuously comply with applicable laws and regulations, or breaches
any employment contract, agreement or internal rules and regulations of our Group;
(ii) the employment relationship between the Participant and our Group is terminated pursuant to
any circumstance specified under Article 39 of the PRC Labour Contract Law;
(iii) the Participant breaches this Agreement or otherwise causes material losses to each of the
Incentive Platforms; or
(iv) the Participant breaches any intellectual property agreement, confidentiality agreement or
non-competition agreement entered into with our Group.
For the avoidance of doubt, the forfeiture by each of the Incentive Platforms of the relevant incentive
interests and distributable profits shall not be deemed to discharge the Participant from all liabilities for
breach, compensation or indemnification, and each of the Incentive Platforms and our Group shall reserve
the right to further claim compensation or indemnification against such Participant in accordance with law.
8. Realization of Incentive Interest
Following the expiry of the lock-up period, and subject to the lock-up undertakings provided by the
Participants at the request of the relevant regulatory authorities, the Participants may dispose of and
monetize their partnership interests after the Company’s listing through the following methods:
(i) during a designated period each year, the Incentive Platforms shall solicit from the Participants
their respective intended quantities of indirect shareholdings in the Company they wish to
dispose of within that year;
(ii) upon collecting the disposal intentions from the Participants, and subject to the decision-
making and disclosure procedures required by the relevant stock exchange, the Incentive
Platforms shall, within six months, determine whether to proceed with the disposal of Shares.
If proceeding, they shall determine the disposal method, proportion, and price based on
prevailing market conditions. The Participants shall not have the right to object to such
decisions;
(iii) if a disposal is carried out, the average disposal price per Share shall be calculated on an
arithmetic basis, taking into account the total number of Shares disposed of and the net disposal
proceeds during the disposal period (i.e., the gross proceeds less actual expenses and any taxes
or fees borne by the Incentive Platforms);
